Nothing here is "current state" — it is how the system got here.** As of the 2026-08-14 restructure, `SESSION_REFERENCE.md` holds **no narrative at all**: every session's story is written directly here at wrap-up, and the hub keeps only current, non-derivable state under a hard 250-line cap (#401).

## 2026-08-17 (2nd) — Post-ship reconcile: the hub's version stamps, and three UNTESTED items that reached main with nowhere to land

**Doc-only, branch `docs/post-ship-reconcile`, BOTH repos.** No code, no migrations, no deploy. Opened by auditing the ROI-skip branch *after* it merged — the audit found three defects that a correct-looking wrap-up had left behind, none of which the shipping session did anything wrong to cause.

**Superseded hub values** (all three were stamped `(v: 2026-08-17)` while carrying pre-deploy values): `vfo-admin-api` **v749 → v750** · `live-149-roi-skip-reschedule` → **`live-150-tax-step-dates`** · `backend-good-2026-08-16-v748` → **`backend-good-2026-08-17-v750`**. Re-derived and unchanged: action count 463, `deno check` 0, 15 crons all active, 8 pipelines LIVE, 186 notification rules, 162 `client_tax_plans` columns, security advisor GREEN against the documented baseline, hub 214 lines before this pass.

**1. The stamps were stale by construction, not by carelessness (#408).** `SESSION_WRAPUP.md` puts the save-point tag LAST *so it cannot go stale* — but the hub's DERIVE expectations are written in Part 1A, three parts before the deploy happens and the tag exists. Following the prompt exactly therefore stamps today's date against the version and tag you arrived with. That is worse than an old date: the hub's own preamble makes a stamp mean "confirmed on this date", so the single signal a reader has for spotting drift is the one that gets falsified — on the three lines a new session reads first. Fixed by ordering: those three lines now carry an inline instruction to re-stamp after Part 4D. Every other DERIVE expectation is knowable in Part 1 and stays there.

**2. Three UNTESTED items reached `main` with no landing place.** The first chat's handoff carried them; `grep` on the shipped docs returned zero hits for all three. The wrap-up's rule 5 reconciled OWED/WATCH/PARKED and never mentioned UNTESTED, so a field designed to survive a handoff had nowhere to go at the far end. **The prompt was already fixed in [#238](docs/prompts/SESSION_WRAPUP.md)**; this entry records the *data* half — all three are now OWED: the `retainer_first` route was click-tested BEFORE the later `save-task` / `invoice-receipt` / `revshare-sweep` / `confirmation-email` edits landed and has had no run since, the decline path on a `meeting_first` plan was never walked, and `overview-tax.ts`'s positional reorder has never been viewed in Client Overview. The earlier entry's *"click-tested end to end, 9/9 bells"* is true of `meeting_first` only.

**3. The smoke gate was green against v749 while v750 shipped.** Recorded nowhere, now OWED. It is a wiring check, so the exposure is narrow — but v750 touched `overview-tax.ts`, and if the next deploy's gate fails, the cause is as likely to be v750's change as that deploy's.

**Nothing was discharged from OWED this pass** — this is a net +3, which is what an audit that finds real gaps looks like. The prompt's own rule ("an OWED list that only grows is a broken list") is about sessions that never close items, not about the audit that opens them honestly.

## 2026-08-17 — A second way to skip the ROI meeting, and completion dates that showed the future

**Branch `claude/vfo-session-setup-3f44e2` BOTH repos, across two chats.** `vfo-admin-api` v748 → **v749** (the meeting-first backend, deployed mid-branch) → **v750 pending** (the Client Overview date mirror, committed but not yet deployed at the time of writing). `boldsign-webhook` untouched at **v40**; `draft-agreement-pdfs` v1. **Action count unchanged at 463** — both halves changed existing handlers only. Three migrations, all applied via MCP **and** committed as files (#196). `deno check --no-lock` **0**, `npm run build` exit 0 (33 route pages), security advisor **GREEN against the exact documented baseline**.

**Superseded hub values:** `client_tax_plans` 161 columns → **162** (`roi_skip_mode`) · `notification_rules` 184 rows → **186** (Tax Planners area +2). Unchanged and re-derived this session: action count 463, 15 cron jobs all active, all 8 pipelines LIVE, 33 route pages, `boldsign-webhook` v40.

### 1. "Skip ROI meeting" becomes two routes

The skip shipped on 2026-08-16 assumed one ordering: the client decides, signs and pays, and only then is the detailed tax plan meeting booked. Real engagements also run the other way round — the meeting happens **first**, and the decision, signing and payment follow it. One button could not express that, and forcing the meeting-first cases through the retainer-first sequence asked the wrong people for the wrong things in the wrong order.

**The shape chosen, and why.** A discriminator column `client_tax_plans.roi_skip_mode text` sits **beside** the existing one-way `roi_meeting_skipped_at` rather than replacing it or adding a parallel timestamp. Both buttons still stamp the original column, so **every mechanism keyed on "was it skipped?" is route-blind and was not touched** — the skipped-away rows, Tax 2's green Done 1/1, the `ready-for-tax3.ts` refusal, the `|skipped` email template axis, the `overview-tax.ts` `applicable` mirror. Only four FE step gates and the bell sequence read the mode. **NULL reads as `retainer_first` everywhere**, so any pre-column row keeps the behaviour it was created under; no backfill was needed, because at the time no live plan had been skipped. **No CHECK constraint** — no column on that table has one, and `skip-roi-meeting.ts` is the sole writer and validates the value, so widening the set later is a deploy rather than a migration.

**One action, one new parameter.** `automation_TAX_skiproimeeting` takes `mode`; absent means `retainer_first`, unrecognised is a 400. A second click on the **other** route is a **refusal, not a silent no-op** — the routes unlock different steps and have already asked different people for different things, so nobody may believe they changed it. The FE grew a second light-green button; both keep their `confirm()`, whose text now spells out the ordering, and the skipped booking row's chip **names the route** (`ROI meeting skipped — meeting first`) because the two are otherwise indistinguishable on that row.

**Two new notification rules, and the title decision behind them** (`20260817100100_…` sort 31, `20260817100200_…` sort 32, both `ALLOCATED_TAX_PLANNER` / `action_required`). `TAX_roi_skipped_hlm_ready` deliberately **shares** its title with `TAX_planner_hlm_ready` — same instruction, same person, different route — so the existing `clearHlmConfirmBells` retires it untouched. `TAX_roi_skipped_decision1_ready` needed its **own** title, `Complete Client decision 1 for`, and this is the part that would have shipped broken: on the meeting-first route the shared `Complete the tax plan review steps for%` prefix is satisfied by the **presentation alone**, so raising the decision-1 ask under it would have cleared the bell on the next clear-site run, before anyone read it. Two asks separated in time need two titles. Written up as **#407**.

**Route-aware wording, including one FYI.** `revshare-sweep.ts` asks a meeting-first planner for the presentation **only** — naming Client decision 1 there would make the bell unperformable (it is still locked behind the retainer) and waiting on it would make it unretirable. `confirmation-email.ts`'s **dismissible** FYI to Tray was telling her the planner had been asked to schedule a meeting **that had already happened**; auditing only `dismissible:false` bells had missed it, which is the lesson recorded in #407.

**Backend refusals behind every new FE lock (#403).** `decision.ts` 400s on a meeting-first plan whose presentation is unanswered; `postreview-decision.ts` 400s until `retainer_invoice_email_sent` is true, with the **idempotent already-decided return kept FIRST** so a double-submit that in fact succeeded can never fall into the new gate. `overview-tax.ts` additionally **reorders** the two Tax 4 meeting steps ahead of the Tax 3 decision, because `computeTrack` is strictly positional — widening `applicable` alone would have left the wrong `next_action` for the entire pre-payment window and then raised a false skipped-step warning against the steps that genuinely came first.

**Click-tested end to end** on plan 136 (Test Client 59524, program 4): 9/9 bells correct including the sweep's presentation-only wording. Plan 136 is now consumed (real decision, payment and revshare) — a fresh meeting-first test needs a **new plan, not a reset**.

### 2. Completion dates that showed a date in the future

Reported from real data: Dave Clarenbach 59473-003's *"Detailed tax plan meeting confirmation email"* step, sent 08/14, displayed **08/28** — the date of the meeting it books. Three of the tax tab's bespoke step renderers were filling the completion-date column from a field that is not a completion date at all: `tax_hlm_confirm` read `tax4_meeting_date` (always future), `tax_presentation_link` read `presentation_send_date` (the scheduled send day, shown **even before the step was done**), and `tax_returns_request` preferred `requested_at` over `received_at`. Every ordinary step reads `client_tax_progress.completed_date` and was always correct, as is every step in the MAP 1 / PIP / Regular / PFT tabs — the defect is confined to renderers that have no progress row and must therefore name their stamp by hand.

**The design call on the presentation step.** It now pins to `presentation_scheduled_at` and **does not move when the sweep later sends** — scheduling is the human's work on that step; the send is the system's. This is **deliberately the inverse** of what `overview-tax.ts` did, so the backend mirror was flipped to match in the same change rather than left to drift (#339): the two had been disagreeing by a day on any plan whose sweep ran the morning after scheduling, silently, because both dates were plausible.

**Where a stamp is missing, blank beats a wrong date.** 13 plans carry a meeting date with no `tax4_meeting_confirm_email_sent_at`, all dated through `automation_TAX_save_meeting_date` — an action still dispatched and gated but with **zero frontend callers**, which is why they exist. They now show an empty cell with the green dot and the meeting still on the chip, matching what Client Overview already reported for them. Neither a backfill nor the removal of that dead action was done; both are flagged, not actioned.

Verified against seven live cases (Clarenbach, Hurdle, Slosser's legacy blank, Betalleluz, Yamamoto, Moran) plus a scheduled-but-unsent fixture built on test client 59524 and deleted afterwards. Written up as **#406**.

## 2026-08-16 — Skipping the ROI meeting, returns already on file, and nine confirmation emails that can be moved

**Branch `claude/vfo-session-setup-b21ded` BOTH repos. `vfo-admin-api` v744 → **v748** (four deploys, each ACTIVE-confirmed); `boldsign-webhook` untouched at **v40**; `draft-agreement-pdfs` v1. Action count **461 → 463**. Four migrations, all applied via MCP `apply_migration` **and** committed as files (#196). `deno check --no-lock` **0**, `npm run build` exit 0 (33 route pages), security advisor re-verified **GREEN against the exact documented baseline after the DDL**, 5-pipeline smoke gate **5/5 after every one of the four deploys**.**

**Superseded hub values:** `vfo-admin-api` v744 → v748 · action count 461 (6 + 455) → 463 (6 + 457) · `client_tax_plans` 160 columns → 161 · `notification_rules` 183 rows → 184 (Tax area 36 → 37) · `email_templates` gains ids 220–225. Unchanged and re-derived: 15 cron jobs all active, all 8 pipelines LIVE, 33 route pages, 11 `send_mode=true` template rows.

### 1. "Already have tax returns" (v745)

The "Request Tax Returns" step assumed the returns had to be asked for. Often they are already on file, and emailing the client for something we hold is noise. A second light-blue **one-click** button (no confirm — nothing irreversible happens) fires the new `automation_TAX_returns_already_have` (`actions/tax/returns-already-have.ts`, `ADMIN_ONLY_ACTIONS`, dispatched beside `request_returns`). It stamps **only** `tax_returns_received_at` — no email, no Gmail draft, no `tax_upload_token` minted, `tax_returns_requested_at` stays NULL — and is idempotent so a second click cannot move the date shown on the step.

**It fires the same bell as an upload, on purpose.** With no planner allocated it raises `TAX_returns_allocate_team_member` to Tracy + Tray under the **identical title prefix** `Allocate a team member for`, differing only in the message ("…are already on file…"). The clear site (`allocate-planner.ts`) matches on the prefix, so any divergence there would have stranded the bell (#365). Fail-soft: the stamp is what the caller waits on.

**One deliberate divergence from the upload path:** `upload-notify.ts` stamps every unstamped plan the client holds, so one upload can green both programs; this button stamps **only the plan whose tab is open**. A both-programs client is therefore clicked once per program tab — the admin is asserting a fact about the plan in front of them. The done pill reads **"Returns on file"** with the date in the date column when the step was never requested.

### 2. Skip ROI meeting — and skipping is FINAL (v746)

Some clients go straight to the detailed tax plan meeting. There was no way to record that, so the whole Tax 2 phase sat open forever and the plan looked stalled. New column `client_tax_plans.roi_meeting_skipped_at` (`20260816230000_tax_roi_skip_column.sql`) and new action `automation_TAX_skiproimeeting` (`actions/tax/skip-roi-meeting.ts`, `ADMIN_ONLY_ACTIONS`). The button is light green and **keeps its `confirm()`** precisely because the action is irreversible — the contrast with the one-click button above is the rule: confirm what cannot be undone.

**Guards, then one write:** already-skipped → no-op **without re-stamping**; already booked (`tax3_meeting_date` or `ready_for_tax3_decision='Yes'`) → 400; no planner allocated → 400 (the same ownership rule the confirm send uses). Then the stamp, and everything after it is fail-soft in one try/catch — a bell must never fail a skip that is already written.

**The bell hygiene is most of the work.** Every ask that pointed at a now-skipped step would otherwise sit unretirable in someone's inbox. The handler clears legacy `Book the ROI meeting for%`, runs the **review-outcome matrix exactly as booking does** (a recorded Proceed clears — program 4 only once Green/Red also reads Proceed; a recorded Stop clears because skipping and carrying on overrides the recommendation), clears the planner's `Enter the tax planning opportunities for%` and the PF's `Download the ROI presentation for%`, then fires the new rule **`TAX_roi_skipped_decision_needed`** (`20260816230100_…`, sort 222, `ASSIGNED_PF`, action-required) to the assigned PF — fallback Tracy, routed on the **portal login** address via `taxPfLoginEmail`, not the correspondence map. Title prefix **`Complete the Client tax planning decision for`** is load-bearing: registered in the `utils/tax-review-bell.ts` header map, exported as `ROI_SKIPPED_DECISION_PREFIX`, cleared by `clearRoiSkippedDecisionBells`. **Satisfied-on-fire guard:** a plan that already carries a `tax_decision` gets no bell, because the only clear site has already run. **Cleared ONLY by `decision.ts`**, on any decision, immediately after the common UPDATE every branch passes through.

**One-way-ness is what makes the rest safe.** `ready-for-tax3.ts` 400s **both** decisions on a skipped plan, so there is no un-skip and no later booking. That is what lets `save-task.ts` widen `roiBooked` to **`roiSettled`** (booked OR skipped) in both the `alreadySatisfied` guard and the Green/Red clear, and Tray's Proceed bell messages now end "…or skip the ROI meeting if the client is moving straight to the detailed tax plan meeting" on both programs.

**The display split is the part worth remembering (#405).** Skipping removes five steps — the four Tax 2 steps plus Tax 3's `ROI Presentation` — but they do **not** share one done-rule. `tax_3_decision` (the booking step) **counts as DONE** because "there will be no meeting" is a real answer to it, which is what leaves **Tax 2 reading a green Done 1/1** on the card and in the hero rather than an empty phase; the other four drop out of the counts and render grey `Skipped` rows — **but only when unanswered**, since work actually done before the skip still counts. The booking row shows a green dot, a green `ROI meeting skipped` chip and the stamp date. Skipped rows render on **every** surface, member and planner included. `overview-tax.ts` mirrors the same five with `applicable: reach && !roiSkipped`, which required giving `ROI Presentation` its own named branch — it had been falling through to the generic `else` (#339). The `Client tax planning decision` gate became `!roiPresentationDone && !roiSkipped`.

### 3. Skip-aware decision emails (v748)

Skipped-ROI clients were being thanked for a meeting that never happened and pointed at a presentation that was never sent. Six new `email_templates` rows, ids **220–225**, all Draft: `TAX_decision_undecided|skipped`, `TAX_decision_decline|skipped`, `TAX_agreementsent|Yes|skipped` and each one's ` (member signing/paying on clients behalf)` variant (`20260816233000_…`). The copy edits: the subject drops "Meeting", meeting-attended phrasing becomes "taking the time to explore tax planning", and the whole presentation-link sentence is removed.

New util `utils/tax-decision-template.ts` `pickDecisionTemplate()` resolves **two independent axes → four names per step** and **returns the name that actually resolved**, because that name is what `gmailDraftFetch` needs to resolve the per-template Draft/Send toggle — handing it a requested-but-missing name would apply the wrong row's send mode (#207/#356). A missing or inactive `|skipped` row falls back to the non-skipped name **keeping the member suffix**, so a member-paying plan can never fall back onto the client-addressed copy. Wired into `decision.ts` (Undecided + No) and `send-agreement.ts` (Yes).

**A typo fix rode along** (`20260816233100_…`): row 20 (`TAX_agreementsent|Yes`, client-paying) read "I also attach a link your presentation". Spotted while copying that body for the `|skipped` variant — which deletes the sentence entirely, so the fix had to land on the normal-case row or it would never have landed at all. Idempotent, body only; the member twin (row 129) was already correct.

### 4. Reschedule / resend meeting confirmations — nine sites, five pipelines (v746/v747)

One pattern: after a send, the pill gains **Reschedule** (or "Edit date" / "Resend with new date") which reopens the same date/time/timezone form pre-filled and re-sends the SAME template. The sites: (i) Tax 4 `tax_hlm_confirm` — FE-only, its handler already re-armed the planner reminder; (ii) Tax 2 `tax_3_decision` booked pill — `ready-for-tax3.ts` nulls `tax3_assess_reminder_sent_at` when the date genuinely changes and a reminder had been stamped; (iii) MAP 1 PIP 1 / Follow-up — the slot lives in the task notes string, so the notes slot is re-written and `parseSlotNotes` pre-fills; (iv) Regular MAP 4 confirm — which **also now persists the slot into progress notes on first send** via `msm_save_priority_task`, where previously it was stored nowhere; (v) PIP Meetings tab — uses the handler's existing prefill/diff; (vi) PFT Meetings 1–3; (vii) Specialist Stage 1; (viii) Specialist Stage 2 "Resend with new date"; (ix) MAP 4 meeting-date step, now editable.

**The durable lesson is #404: re-invoking a send handler re-arms every reminder ladder it stamps, silently.** So the frontend passes `reschedule: true` and each ladder-arming side effect sits behind `!reschedule` — `pft/meeting-email.ts` keeps the discovery link but skips `discovery_email_sent_at` / `discovery_pf_notified_at`; `onboarding/prelim-email.ts` skips `sif_email_sent_at` (and the FE does not `advanceStage`); `onboarding/stage2-email.ts` skips Tracy's revenue-share bell. **Three sites deliberately DO re-arm, and the discriminator is the direction the delay counts:** the Tax 2 assess reminder counts *down to* the meeting (#359) so a moved meeting must invalidate it; MAP 4's `map4-set-meeting-date.ts` clears `map4_followup_sent_at` / `map4_reminder_sent_at` / `map4_stall_notified_at` on a genuine date change (**user-approved** — a moved MAP 4 meeting should re-draft the follow-up ladder); and Tax 4's confirm already nulled its guard on every send.

**Stage 2 needed a second mechanism.** A resend that logs its meeting must edit the row, not file a new one, so `save_onboarding_meeting` gained an optional **`meeting_id`** that switches it from INSERT to a scoped UPDATE (row must belong to the named onboarding, else 404; only supplied keys written) — **no new action**. The affordance is offered on the **newest logged meeting only**; earlier rows are settled history. `stage2-email.ts` skips the Tracy bell on reschedule.

**Accepted consequence, common to all nine:** rescheduling a send originally made as "date not arranged" **upgrades that record to confirmed**. Reviewed and accepted rather than guarded.

### 5. The decline lock (v747)

`tax_hlm_confirm` was **clickable on a declined plan**. Root cause, and it is the kind that survives testing: the FE gate read `locked: !tax3AipcDone`, and `tax3AipcDone` is deliberately **true** when `tax_decision='No'` or `tax_final_decision='No'`, because a decline *is* the Tax 3 cascade's terminal state. So the predicate meaning "settled" was a union of *completed* and *abandoned*, and the lock derived from it unlocked exactly the closed plans while correctly locking the live mid-cascade ones. On every happy path the gate behaved.

Fixed by **ordering**: the decline test now runs first with its own hint ("Tax planning was declined"), and only then the completion test. Because a UI lock is choreography (#353/#390), `highlevel-meeting-confirm.ts` also 400s `"Tax planning was declined for this plan"` off the same two columns — that is the boundary. Bell-strand check was clean: `TAX_planner_hlm_ready` fires only on the paid Yes track, so locking the step made no action-required bell unperformable. Generalised as **#403**.

### How it was verified

Full click-through on **Test Client (plan 135)** across both programs — the already-have button (bell fires, no email, no token), the skip (Tax 2 greens at 1/1, four grey Skipped rows, the PF bell arrives, `ready-for-tax3` refuses afterwards), a decision on a skipped plan (correct `|skipped` template resolved, PF bell retired), the decline lock from both directions, and each reschedule site. `tax-revshare-sweep-daily` was **manually triggered once** to prove the assess-reminder re-arm and confirm no collateral: a single bell, nothing else. **Smoke gate 5/5 after each of v745, v746, v747 and v748.** Security advisor re-run after the DDL and matched the documented baseline exactly (5 × deny-all `rls_enabled_no_policy` INFO + the `pg_net` WARN).

### Flagged, not built

`decision.ts` writes `tax_decision` **unconditionally**. A backwards re-submit to **No** on a plan whose retainer is already paid would strand that plan's live action-required bells with no clear site left to retire them. No guard was added and no accidental click-path reaches it; recorded as OPEN in the hub. New gotchas this session: **#403** (a terminal outcome satisfies a completion gate), **#404** (a resend re-arms ladders unless flagged), **#405** (the skip-state done-math split).

## 2026-08-14 (SEVENTH session) — The docs stopped being a thing nobody could read

**Branch `docs/session-context-diet` BOTH repos. DOC-ONLY plus two edge code COMMENTS. No behaviour changed anywhere: no handler logic, no migration, no DDL, no DML, no deploy. `vfo-admin-api` stayed **v744**, `boldsign-webhook` **v40**, action count **461 (6 + 455)**, `deno check --no-lock` **0**.**

**The problem, stated honestly.** `SESSION_REFERENCE.md` had grown to **756 lines / 324 KB (~70k tokens)** while its own header ordered every session to read it *in full*. That instruction had been unfulfillable for weeks — the file exceeded a single read — so every session silently skimmed, and skimming is what let false claims live in it indefinitely. The audit that opened this session found, in the hub alone: a Stripe-chain paragraph still describing a **Tax 4 24h auto-lock removed weeks earlier** (its own registry entry, #264, said so); an **OWED list that was already discharged in full** (v744 deployed, `live-148` and `backend-good-2026-08-14-v744` both in git); a helper edge function (`boldsign-template-fields`) **deleted from Supabase with no doc trace**; and `index.ts` described as 88 lines when it is 123.

**What was built.** The hub was rebuilt to **206 lines against a hard 250-line cap**, structured as: the SECURITY INVARIANTS box (**verbatim, unshortened**), a `DERIVE AT SESSION START` command block, LIVE STATE containing *only* what no command can produce (OWED / WATCH / PARKED / STANDING / access-list pointers), a compact SYSTEM MAP, 36 curated always-applies gotchas, a **DOC MAP** of when-to-read triggers, and the verification gate. Every fact that survived was **live-verified on the way in** (MCP, git, greps, `information_schema`) and carries a `(v: 2026-08-14)` freshness stamp. **Nothing was deleted** — displaced prose moved here verbatim under the relocation heading below, the server-to-server chain inventory became the new **`architecture/07-server-chains.md`** (202 lines, merged from the hub's chain section *and* the enumeration that used to be embedded in the operator's starter prompt), and the curated gotcha list went **188 → 36** with all 188 still complete in `GOTCHAS.md`.

**The prompts became version-controlled files.** `docs/prompts/SESSION_STARTER.md` (170 lines, from ~260) and `docs/prompts/SESSION_WRAPUP.md` (95 lines) are now the canonical copies the operator pastes from. The starter keeps every battle-tested rail verbatim — PATH GUARDRAIL, GIT/BRANCH SAFETY, SAVE-POINT SYSTEM, WORK RULES, RESPONSE PROTOCOL, the four startup steps, the no-`VITE_API_URL` / no-test-login warnings — and sheds only the ~15-paragraph chain enumeration, now a pointer to 07-server-chains. It gains two things: a mandate to **run the DERIVE block and state the results before any work**, and a **binding DOC MAP** rule (read the named doc before editing an area; fixing a wrong doc is part of the task). The wrap-up keeps its tag-last skeleton and gains the write discipline that keeps the hub small indefinitely: **every edit declared ADD / UPDATE / DELETE / NOOP**, superseded facts moved out in the same pass, freshness stamps only on what was actually checked, narrative written straight to CHANGELOG, OWED reconciled in both directions, the DERIVE block re-run and reconciled, a curated-gotcha **prune** pass beside the append, and **a line count over 250 blocks the commit**.

**The verification sweep is where the real damage showed.** A third agent checked every cheaply-verifiable claim in the on-demand docs against code and the live DB — **34 fixes across 11 files**, all ground-truthed. Highlights: `flows/tax-planning.md` had never absorbed two earlier commits, so it still called `TAX_tax4_decision_needed` live (**DORMANT** since 2026-08-11, replaced by `TAX_planner_tax4_steps_needed`), still listed `TAX_planner_post_meeting` as active (**DORMANT**, no call site), attributed `TAX_planner_decision2_ready` to the wrong handler, and described `presentation-schedule.ts` as clearing nothing when it has cleared bells since v726; `flows/contract-and-payment.md` still documented **Google-Sheets revshare verification removed on 2026-07-01** (`contract-revshare.ts` has zero Sheets references) and claimed one automation was the *only* notification-inserting site when five are; `integrations/stripe.md` said a missing Connect account **skips silently** when #303 made it write a non-terminal status plus an action-required bell. Counts were the other systemic failure — see **#402**. Two edge-repo **code comments** were corrected in passing: `constants/vault-assess-groups.ts` claimed a frontend mirror that does not exist (grep: zero), and `utils/tax-review-bell.ts`, which bills itself as the one place every tax bell prefix lives, was missing #400's `Tax Assessment PDF added for`.

**New gotchas #401 and #402**, both ALWAYS-APPLIES (docs): the hub needs a hard budget and must derive rather than restate; and a count written into prose is a promise nobody keeps — with a file contradicting itself three ways as the tell that nobody has read it end to end.

**Honest limits.** `NOTIFICATION_AUDIT.md` needs **regeneration, not patching** — roughly a third of live rules have no entry and its structure is inherently a count-snapshot; it now carries a live per-area table and a derive-don't-count instruction, and the rebuild is recorded as OWED. Line numbers inside `file:line` references were **not** verified (paths were: 482 of 483 resolve). The Tax 4 dormant-bell rewrites were read from migrations and handlers but **not click-tested**. And the whole exercise is documentation: it changes what a session *knows*, not what the system *does*.

## Relocated from SESSION_REFERENCE during the 2026-08-14 restructure

  - **THE MODEL, IN ONE SENTENCE.** `utils/notify.ts` gained `businessDelayCutoffIso(days)` — a backward walk of whole weekdays from now, with any fractional remainder subtracted as plain hours **afterwards** — and every stall tier in every sweep now calls it instead of the calendar `delayCutoffIso`: `tax/revshare-sweep` (Tax 3 ×6, Tax 4 ×4, Tax 5 ×4), `pipeline/contract-revshare-sweep` (MAP 1 ×6), `advisor/sweep` ×6, `accountant/sweep` ×6, `onboarding/sweep` (14 tiers through one wrapper), `pft/sweep` ×6, `specialist-revenue/payout-sweep` ×5, `pipeline/contract-check-reminder-sweep` (uncleared-check bells + the migration setup-link ladder), `regular/map4-followup-sweep` (3 chained tiers). **The stored `notification_rules.delay_days` numbers were NOT renumbered** — a "2" is still a 2, it is simply counted against a different calendar — which is why nothing needed a data migration and also why **a rule row read in isolation no longer tells you what it means; the caller does** (#396). Two ladders count FORWARD rather than back — the Tax 2 assess-form reminder and the MAP 1 check-payment lookahead — and those use the sibling `businessDayHorizonDateOnly`. `growth/overdue-sweep` has no delay offset at all, so it could not be converted and instead early-returns on Saturday and Sunday UTC ticks.
  - **THE ORDER OF OPERATIONS INSIDE THE HELPER IS THE WHOLE TRICK (#397).** The obvious implementation — subtract `days * 86400000`, then skid backwards off a weekend — is wrong, and wrong in a way that only shows up on the tiers nobody tests. The Notification Editor exposes `delay_days` with `step=0.5`, so fractional delays are reachable from the UI; subtracting the fraction FIRST can move the walk's starting day into Saturday, where the walk then buys back an entire extra weekday, and the result is that a LARGER `days` produces a LATER cutoff than a smaller one. A ladder built on that fires its 4-day PF bell before its 2-day reminder email. Walking whole weekdays first and applying the fraction last keeps the function monotonic, and **monotonicity — not any individual case — is the property that was actually tested**: a pinned-clock script in the scratchpad ran 18 fixed cases plus a **77-sample monotonicity sweep**, all green. That script lives outside both repos and was deliberately not committed.

The live DB half was re-queried directly: templates **33** and **142** no longer match `24 hour`/`24h`/`24-hour`, and both new rules exist enabled at sorts **131/141** with defaults **2** and **4**. The user click-tested the Automation panels, the Notification Editor and its chips, the new rules' visibility, the Tax 5 confirm dialog (cancelled), the Tax 4 confirm dialogs and the Slosser Tax 5 button dialog. **The honest limit: a business-day cutoff is only observable on a real cron tick.** Every gate above is a type check, a build, a grep or a dialog — **the first genuine proof of the conversion is the first Monday sweep after deploy**, which is exactly the tick the change exists to fix.
  - **OWED, in order.** *[ALL FOUR DISCHARGED — verified 2026-08-14 at the SIXTH session's audit against MCP + `git tag -l`, not against this text: v741 shipped (the next session deployed on top of it, 741→742→743) and both `live-147-business-day-reminders` and `backend-good-2026-08-14-v741` exist in git. **This list read as outstanding for a whole session after it was settled — #376, and the reason the LIVE STATE cells must be rewritten from git and MCP, never from the previous cell text.**]* **(1) `supabase functions deploy vfo-admin-api` → v741**, freshness-checked 0-behind in the SAME invocation (#337). **(2) the 5-pipeline smoke gate against v741, in the same sitting** — it was correctly skipped here because nothing shipped and no routing/dispatch/webhook/auth file was opened, but a deploy arms its first trigger. **(3) `npm run deploy`** (14 `src/` files). **(4) tags `live-147-*` and `backend-good-2026-08-14-v741`** — derive N from `git tag -l 'live-*' --sort=v:refname`; `live-146` is the current max. **The backend goes first on purpose.** Until it does, live v740 still contains the 24h auto-charge while the live templates have already stopped promising it; the live UI cannot reach the Proceed branch (its button hardcodes `Undecided`), so the exposure is API-or-legacy-row only — narrow, but real, and the deploy is what closes it rather than merely shipping labels.
- **The Accounting revenue pages printed every slice of every split as a plain dollar figure, which reads as money that has already moved — and most of it had not: a planner's cut with nobody allocated, a member share held for a missing Connect account, a failed transfer waiting on the nightly retry and a payment still clearing all looked exactly like cash in the bank; every share-showing panel now says which slices have actually paid out, the Tax pages gained the Tax Planner column that had been silently folded into VFO income, and chasing one number through the MAP 1 card turned up a real display bug that had been understating VFO's own income by half on member-contribution rows** (2026-08-13/14, the **FIFTH** session dated 2026-08-13 and wrapped up on the 14th, branch `claude/vfo-session-setup-617e7c` BOTH repos — react = **11 modified + 1 NEW `src/` file**, edge = **4 modified files, no new file** + docs. **+0 actions (461)** — nothing registered, so `router/dispatch.ts`, `constants/role-gates.ts`, `index.ts`, `middleware/auth.ts` and `router/webhooks.ts` were **ALL never opened**, the second session running. **Backend DEPLOYED TWICE, each user-approved and each freshness-checked 0-behind in the same invocation (#337): v738 → v739 → v740**, both re-verified **ACTIVE** via MCP. `boldsign-webhook` UNTOUCHED at **v40**. **ZERO DB CHANGES — no migration, no DDL, no DML, not one write**; the security advisor was therefore **not required** and was run anyway as insurance → **GREEN** (documented baseline exactly). `deno check --no-lock` **0**. `npm run build` **exit 0, 33 route pages**. **Pipeline smoke gate DELIBERATELY NOT RUN for either deploy — reasoning recorded in the LIVE STATE row.** Gotchas **#394** + **#395**, both ALWAYS-APPLIES (money); **#134 AMENDED in place** rather than duplicated. **OWED: `npm run deploy` (12 files) + a `live-N` tag, and `backend-good-2026-08-14-v740`.** **MERGE-PENDING (both repos).**)
  - **THE MODEL, IN ONE SENTENCE.** A new `src/components/admin/shareLegState.jsx` maps a leg's **payout column** to a `{note, tone}` — `paid` / `money mapping` / `no share due` / `awaiting payout setup` / `awaiting planner` / `failed — retrying` / `in progress` / `payment clearing` / `awaiting client decision` / `not yet paid` — and three render helpers (`ShareCell` / `PendingNote` / `SubNote`) apply it: a pending amount dims to 0.55 opacity and carries a 9px amber `#b9451d` note, totals and reconciliation aggregates gain a `$X pending` sub-note, and the Received column notes a payment that is merely processing or check-pending. **It is annotation ONLY — no amount, filter or total is derived from any of it** (a comment at the top of the file says so), which is what makes a change this wide safe on money pages.
  - **THE COLUMNS ARE A PROJECTION AND THE VOCABULARY IS INCONSISTENT ON PURPOSE (#395).** The dollar figures were always arithmetic computed at render; the per-leg payout column is the only thing that knows whether money moved. Those columns do not speak one language: a strategic leg carries **BOTH** `'N/A'` (engine) and `'N/A — No Share Due'` (migration backfill, #362/#277), so a terminal check knowing only one of them reports a settled leg as pending forever. `pip_rev_share_status`'s `'Pending'` ambiguously means in-flight **and** failed, and the richer `revPaidValue` the handler computes is **never persisted** — a schema gap, flagged and not fixed. A blank leg is not one state either: on the tax **retainer** it means the share has not fired yet because it fires on the client's decision after the review, not on the charge, which is why that one row carries a `tax_retainer` context and reads *awaiting client decision*.
  - **THE BUG THE USER FOUND BY READING A CARD (#394).** Chasing **Sreenivasulu Vengala** (`pipeline_map1` id **110**: net 2700, gross 5400, `member_contribution` 2700) showed VFO **$337.50** per installment where the engine keeps **$675**. Two display surfaces gross-prorated shares while the installments are **net** dollars — correct on every ordinary row, wrong on exactly the rows where a member had contributed. The engine never did that: **MEMBER pays in full** (cumulative-difference split, never scaled by net/gross, because the entered share is already net of the contribution — #304), **STRATEGIC is gross-prorated**, and **VFOS is a RESIDUAL of the net installment**, never a proration, because nothing is ever transferred for it. So a contribution leaves *more* with VFO, not less. Fixed in `Map1PricingSplitCard.jsx` (VFO row is now the residual, gated on any split being entered, plus a new "Member contribution" stat cell and a gross caption reading *before member contribution*) and in the MAP 1 block of `actions/payments/normalize.ts` (member uses the engine's cumulative math, vfo is the residual, `strategic_partner_share` newly read — its callers `select("*")`, so no loader change was needed; null-vs-0 semantics preserved). **The engine and the DB were always right — this was display-only, no money moved.** Blast radius checked against **all 30 production rows**: only ids **110** and **120**, the only two with a contribution, render differently.
  - **THE BACKEND DID NOTHING BUT WIDEN THREE SELECT LISTS.** `tax-load.ts`, `load.ts` and `pip-load.ts` had been returning payloads the panels rendered *without* their payout columns — the panels were annotating from data they had never been sent. v739 added them (tax also gains `total_fee` / `tax_planner_share` / `tax_planner_id` / `legacy_source`, which is what makes the new **Tax Planner column** computable at all — a per-payment slice prorated dollars-of-TOTAL per the `PricingSplitCard` convention #252, with the **historic-retainer guard** that a migrated plan's stored split describes the implementation only, so its retainer pays the planner nothing). Elite VFO Income became `amount − member − strategic − planner`; **the member and strategic math was not touched.** One instructive near-miss: `SpecialistReconciliationPanel` had been **loading `payout_status` per line and discarding it** — a column arriving in a payload is not the same as a surface reading it, so grep the panel, not just the loader.
  - **THE MEMBER COLUMN SPLIT, AND WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY LEFT ALONE.** Revenue panels now carry **"Member Revenue Share"** and **"Member Money Mapping"** as separate columns (routed by the member's `revenue_decision === 'Money Mapping'`, with the note reading *credited* in the MM column); Reconciliation headers were renamed to match, `"Strategic"` / `"Strategic Share"` became **"Strategic Partner Revenue Share"** including both reconciliation footers' prose, and a zero member slice renders a faint `—` rather than `$0.00` everywhere. **Not touched, deliberately:** `SpecialistRecurringPanel` **cannot** be annotated — `specialist_revenue_recurring_lines` has **no `payout_status` column** at all, so it needs schema work first and was flagged rather than built; `SpecialistRevenuePanel`/`RequestRow` and `AllPaymentsTab` were already status-aware; and the membership / GC / outstanding-links / licence / BG panels have no share columns to annotate.
  - **Verification, and what it does NOT cover.** `deno check --no-lock` → **exit 0**, no `deno.lock` (#112). Parity **6 + 455 = 461, +0** via the documented anchored patterns on the edge worktree. `npm run build` → **exit 0, 33 route pages**. MCP at audit: **`vfo-admin-api` v740 ACTIVE, `boldsign-webhook` v40 ACTIVE, `verify_jwt=false` on both**. **Security advisor RUN → GREEN** (deny-all INFO x5 + `pg_net` WARN only) despite zero DDL. **The user click-verified both deploys through the real Accounting pages and the Payments tab** — which is how the Vengala bug was found, and how the fix was re-verified afterwards. **Honest coverage limits, three of them:** the **PIP** annotation has never been exercised against a real row (there are **zero production PIP purchases**), so it is verified by construction only; the **'awaiting client decision'** note on the tax retainer is derived from *context*, not from any column that says so, and will read wrong the day the retainer share starts firing on the charge; and the smoke gate would have been a weak proof here anyway — it asserts HTTP 200 + no `error`, so a select-list widening returning the wrong columns would still pass it.
  - **OWED.** **`npm run deploy`** in `vfo-react` — **12 `src/` files**, and note that **the entire user-visible feature set is frontend**: v739/v740 are live but invisible, carrying extra payload fields nobody reads. **The uncomfortable corollary is that the Vengala proration bug is still wrong on live until that deploy happens** — it is display-only and no money is affected, but an admin reading the MAP 1 card today still sees $337.50 where the engine keeps $675. Then a **`live-N`** tag — **derive N from `git tag -l 'live-*' --sort=v:refname`, do NOT assume; `live-145` is the current max** — and **`backend-good-2026-08-14-v740`** on the merged edge main commit. **Flagged, not built:** a `payout_status` column on `specialist_revenue_recurring_lines` (the one panel that cannot be annotated), and persisting `pip_rev_share_status`'s richer `revPaidValue` so PIP can distinguish in-flight from failed. **Carried-in and unchanged:** the Outstanding Payment Links "Resend email" click-test, #327, #333, #335, #338, #359, the **Aug 6 specialist payout that fired twice (~$1,382)**, #370, and the **PARKED** #384. **Watch item unchanged: Steve Bitzer's Sep 4 installment.**

Converted in **v672**; the claim is now literally true, and `grep -rn "pipeline_sandbox_config" actions/migration/` must stay at ZERO. `migration_stripe_lookup` takes an OPTIONAL `client_id` (null → global config) which the admin tab now passes.** Gotchas #251 + #302.
- **Frontend UX layer** (live as of 2026-05-27): `src/lib/api.js` is **113 lines** and exports the original `callApi` / `getSession` / `setSession` / `clearSession` PLUS a module-level promise cache: `loadCachedData()` (caches `load_data`), `loadCachedAction(action, payload)` (keyed cache for other reads — used for `msm_load_programs`, `msm_load_training_track`, `msm_load_client_track`), `clearCachedData()`, `clearActionCache()`. Cache invalidates on `clearSession`. `callApi` enforces a **TWO-TIER `AbortController` timeout** via `timeoutFor(action)` (2026-08-03): **`automation_*` WRITE actions get 60s (`SLOW_WRITE_TIMEOUT_MS`)**, reads and everything else keep **20s (`REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS`)**, and the thrown message reports whichever limit applied. The long tier exists because a client-side abort does NOT stop the edge function — a false 20s timeout on a long automation chain produced a "try again" that the user acted on, double-drafting a Gmail email (gotcha **#319**). Reads matching `^load_|_load(_|$)` (plus explicit `vault_list`) auto-retry once on timeout, writes never retry on timeout (prevents double-writes — #30, untouched). The **Skeleton library** lives in the `src/components/shared/skeletons/` package (rebuilt 2026-07-02): `primitives.jsx` (Skeleton bar, SkeletonRow/Card/Stats, CardShell, HeroSkeleton, ListHeader/SearchFilter/Table/TokenForm skeletons) composed into page skeletons grouped by area — `admin.jsx` (DirectoryList, AutomationTracker, AccountingTable, EmailTemplates, MemberOverview, StrategicPartners, Onboarding list/detail, MemberProfileDetails, AdminMsmHome, AdminProgramView, ProgramNotes), `tracks.jsx` (Map1/PFT/Training tracks, TaxPlanList, PIP list/detail, PhaseList, ClientsList, CoachingMeetings/Renewal, MsmHome, CiqList), `portal.jsx` (Showroom, VaultSections/VaultRows, SharedDocs, MemberProfile). `Skeleton.jsx` re-exports the whole package for back-compat — import from either path. Every loading state in the app renders a page-shaped skeleton (no "Loading…" text anywhere); list skeletons show 2–3 rows; all colors are `var(--vfo-*)` so they theme in dark mode. Shimmer keyframes live in `src/index.css` (`.vfo-skeleton` + `vfo-skeleton-shimmer`). **Theming:** `src/lib/theme.js` (`vfo_theme` localStorage key, `usePortalTheme()` in the five portal-level pages, `applyThemeForCurrentRoute()` at boot) — see gotcha #169.

#### ENVIRONMENT GOTCHAS

- **Bash is NOT on PATH** — use PowerShell. `git`, `curl`, `docker`, `psql` all run via PowerShell or `docker exec`.
- **PowerShell does NOT have `tail`** — use `Select-Object -Last N` instead. `| tail -3` will silently break pipelines (the upstream command may not run at all, swallowing output).
- **PowerShell `sort -V` is NOT version-aware** — `sort` aliases `Sort-Object`, which returns LEXICAL order (`live-9` sorts after `live-64`). Derive max tags with `git tag -l 'live-*' --sort=v:refname | Select-Object -Last 1` (gotcha #222).
- **PowerShell mangles JSON inline** — use `--data-binary @file`:
  ```
  '{"action":"foo","x":"y"}' | Out-File tmp.json -Encoding ascii -NoNewline
  curl.exe -s -X POST <url> -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary "@tmp.json"
  Remove-Item tmp.json
  ```
- **PowerShell `Set-Content -Encoding utf8` AND `Out-File -Encoding utf8` both write a UTF-8 BOM** which leaks into commit message subjects (rendered as `﻿` in `git log`) and corrupts box-drawing characters. For bulk file writes AND commit messages:
  ```powershell
  $utf8 = New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding $false
  [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($file, $content, $utf8)
  ```
- The Edit tool handles UTF-8 correctly — prefer it for moderate edits.
- **PowerShell here-string commit messages** can break on quoted text — use `git commit -F <tmpfile>` instead of inline `git commit -m`. AND write the tmpfile BOM-free per the above. The Bash tool's `cat > file << 'EOF'` heredoc avoids this entirely if you're already in a Bash context.
- **`git log --format=%B` in PowerShell collapses newlines into spaces** when piped through a variable — multi-line commit bodies become one long line. If you need to round-trip a message (e.g. to amend), rewrite the original from your prepared text rather than reading it back.
- **Supabase CLI stderr noise** (Bundling Function: …, Setting up Edge Functions runtime…) is benign — PowerShell flags it as RemoteException but it's normal CLI progress.
- **`vite build` stderr noise** (the `[plugin builtin:vite-reporter]` chunk-size warning) is similarly benign — PowerShell flags as RemoteException but the build succeeded. Look for `Published` at the end of `npm run deploy` output to confirm gh-pages push worked.
- **Local DB seed is sparse** — members table for TEST-001 doesn't exist; clients/pipeline_map1/email_templates start empty. Many "save didn't persist" reports are FK-driven seed gaps, not refactor regressions. See `supabase/seed.sql` for what IS seeded.
- **Local DB sequence gap** — `experts.id` has no DEFAULT in the pg_dump baseline; inserts via `save_specialist` against the local DB fail with not-null violation. Pre-existing test-data issue. (Frontend works around it by computing id client-side.)
- **CORS in local-dev** — Kong gateway intercepts OPTIONS preflight and stamps `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`. Production hits the function directly. Don't worry if local CORS smoke shows `*`.
- **`supabase/.temp/cli-latest` shows as modified after any CLI deploy** — Supabase CLI version-tracking artifact, not project code. Exclude from every commit.
- **`supabase storage cp --experimental` rejects absolute and outside-cwd LOCAL paths** with a misleading *"Unsupported operation … between local directories"* — it reads the path as a second local endpoint rather than a filesystem source/target. **Stage the file inside the repo cwd and use a `./relative` path**; that works for both `ss:///bucket/obj ./file` (download) and `./file ss:///bucket/obj` (upload). Used both ways for the 2026-08-12 ROI v3 template round-trip, hash-verified.
- **`gh` (GitHub CLI) is NOT installed on this machine** — PR creation is by URL in the browser, and any "merge it for me" step is a local `git merge --squash` + `git push` instead.
- **GitHub Pages CDN + browser HTML cache** — after `npm run deploy` succeeds (look for `Published`), the live bundle filenames change (e.g. `index-<hash>.js`), but browsers often serve a cached `index.html` that points at the OLD bundle. Confirm the deploy reached the CDN by `curl -s https://vfoportal.com/ | grep -oE 'index-[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.(js|css)'` and comparing to the new filename in the build output. If the live HTML serves the new bundle but the user's browser still shows old content, it's local cache — DevTools → Network → "Disable cache" → reload, or use incognito.

### WHAT'S NOT IN THE SYSTEM (full prose; the hub keeps a one-line summary)

#### WHAT'S NOT IN THE SYSTEM

- No automated tests; no test runner; no `__tests__/`
- No GitHub Actions / CI/CD on either repo
- No frontend TypeScript (only the backend Deno code is `.ts`)
- No Supabase Auth — custom session-token scheme over `admin_sessions` (shared by **all six login types** across **five portals**: admin, member, client, specialist, and — added 2026-07-22 — **tax_planner** [plus the legacy unified `login`]). Passcodes are **salted PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256** (210k iterations) stored in `allowed_admins.passcode_hash` / `member_logins.passcode_hash` / `client_logins.passcode_hash` / `specialist_logins.passcode_hash` / **`tax_planner_logins.passcode_hash`** (the 5th `*_logins` table, keyed on `tax_planner_id`; migration `20260722100000`, gotcha #258). The legacy unsalted-SHA-256 `passcode` column was dropped 2026-05-29 (gotcha #47). **Since 2026-08-10 (v716) four of the five portals — member / specialist / tax planner / client, never admin — carry a self-service passcode reset at `/forgot-password?type=` backed by the PUBLIC `request_password_reset`, which mints a 1-hour `login_setup_tokens` row and auto-sends the `/set-password` link; admin resets stay manual (gotcha #355).
- No React Context — but `src/lib/api.js` DOES hold a small module-level promise cache for read-only actions (caches `load_data` + `msm_load_programs` + `msm_load_*_track` etc. across re-mounts within a session; cache invalidates on `clearSession`). This is different from a state library — it's an in-flight-promise dedupe layer, not a state store.
- DB migrations directory exists at `vfo-edge-functions/supabase/migrations/` (mostly applied via Supabase MCP `apply_migration`, not via CLI auto-management). Five manual-apply SQL files live at `vfo-edge-functions/supabase/cron/{revshare,tax-revshare,chargescheduled,check-reminder,advisor}-sweep.sql` — applied once each to install the daily crons; not auto-managed. PIP Meetings has no cron.
- **Five background jobs** via `pg_cron` (02:00 / 02:30 / 03:00 / 04:00 / 05:00 UTC) — see CURRENT STATE. MAP 1 reminder timers live on `pipeline_map1`: `c14_email_sent_at` (PCADMIN Undecided email — only written on Undecided branch by `automation_PIPFU_decision`), `c17_followup_sent_date` (agreement signing — written by `automation_CONTRACT_sendagreement`), `pay1_email_sent_at` (payment email — written by `automation_CONTRACT_paymentemail`). Each stall has `*_reminder_sent_at` (2-business-day idempotency guard) + `*_pf_notified_at` (4-business-day idempotency guard) — six timestamptz columns total per row. The legacy unimplemented `c14_followup1_sent` / `c17_followup1_sent` / `pay1_followup1_sent` / etc. columns were DROPPED in migration `map1_reminder_ladder_columns` (2026-05-21). The newer `pay{2,3,4}_reminder_sent` columns are unrelated to the reminder ladder — they're **7-BUSINESS-day** pre-due-date nudges for check clients (forward horizon via `businessDayHorizonDateOnly`; the due dates themselves stay calendar), written by `_checkreminder_sweep`. Tax reminder timers live on `client_tax_plans`: Tax 3 uses `tax_decision_reminder_sent_at` / `tax_decision_pf_notified_at` (Undecided email stall), `signed_reminder_sent_at` / `signed_pf_notified_at` (agreement signing stall), `payment_reminder_sent_at` / `payment_pf_notified_at` (payment link stall) — all on the 2-business-day / 4-business-day tier; Tax 4 uses `post_review_reminder_sent_at` / `post_review_pf_notified_at` (**shared by the Continue AND Undecided branches** since the 24h auto-lock was removed, #264; formerly the Continue branch used 24h auto-lock without a reminder column); Tax 5 uses `implementation_reminder_sent_at` / `implementation_pf_notified_at` (**shared by the Proceed AND Undecided branches** as of 2026-08-14, both on the 2-business-day / 4-business-day tier; the Proceed branch's old 24h auto-charge is deleted, #398). The Tax 4 meeting-date nudge (in-app bell to the assigned PF + allocated planner + Tracy) uses `tax4_meeting_date` + `tax4_meeting_reminder_last_sent_at` (fired ONCE per plan; the bell persists until a Tax 4 decision is recorded). Advisor reminder timers live on `advisor_onboarding`: `decision_email_sent_at` (Undecided email stall — also the trigger for the 14-day implicit-No), `agreement_sent_at` (signing stall), `payment_link_sent_at` (payment stall). Each stall has `*_reminder_sent_at` / `*_pf_notified_at` 2-business-day / 4-business-day guards — six timestamptz columns. The 14-day implicit-No rule shares the `decision_email_sent_at` timer with the Undecided reminder but **counts CALENDAR days, deliberately** (#396); it writes `final_decision='Auto-Declined'` + `final_decision_at` and chains `_declineemail`. PIP Meetings has no equivalent timers — there are no client-side reminder paths.
- No structured logging (just `console.log`/`console.error`) — **but frontend errors are now captured by Sentry** (H3, error-monitoring only; `@sentry/react` init in `main.jsx`, reported from `ErrorBoundary`; added 2026-06-18)

It did not. `vault_tax_admin_upload_url` opened with an unconditional `if (!isTaxAdmin(auth.session.email)) return 403`, so an allowlisted planner would have sailed through the middleware and been refused **inside** the handler by a constant naming three humans (`constants/tax-access.ts`). The fix is the branch its read twin `vault_tax_download` had already established — `callerRole === "tax_planner"` → `denyIfNotPlannerClient`, `else` → `isTaxAdmin` — and **the tell that it was needed is that the read twin was shaped that way and the write twin was not.** `vault_gen_upload_url` needed the simpler half: the group guard `vault_gen_download` already carried. **Generalised: before widening any allowlist, grep the target handler for a second gate.**
  - **TWO MINTERS, TWO NAMED CONFINEMENTS (#309).** Both actions added here mint **signed upload URLs**, the exact class #309 says must never sit in a gate list unexamined. Each is now covered twice: `TAX_PLANNER_ALLOWED_ACTIONS` for reachability, and an in-handler `denyIfNotPlannerClient` whole-group scope check that resolves the caller from **their own session token**, never a body value. The object path is built server-side as `<client_id>/<rand>_<safeName>` — **the request body selects neither bucket nor folder**, only a filename that is regex-scrubbed. ## Archived from SESSION_REFERENCE on 2026-08-11 (the tax review/hand-off chain session; login-autofill entry aged out of the hub's most-recent-three)

- **A tax planner was locked out of her own portal over and over, and the backend was innocent â€” her password manager could not identify the login fields, so it kept re-filling the passcode she had just replaced; the five login forms got real autofill identity, and the four non-admin portals got a self-service "forgot passcode" flow so nobody has to wait on an admin for a link again** (2026-08-10, the **THIRD** session that day, branch `claude/vfo-session-setup-ae3110` BOTH repos â€” edge = **1 NEW handler + 2 modified code files + 1 new migration file**, react = **1 NEW page + 11 modified code files** + docs. **+1 action (458)** = **`request_password_reset`** (**PUBLIC**); `constants/role-gates.ts`, `middleware/auth.ts` and `router/webhooks.ts` were **never opened**, `router/dispatch.ts` gained exactly one registration line; parity re-counted at audit = 6 + 452 = 458. **Backend DEPLOYED ONCE, user-approved: v715 â†’ v716**, re-verified **ACTIVE** via MCP `list_edge_functions` at this audit; freshness checked **in the same invocation as the deploy**, 0 behind (#337). `boldsign-webhook` UNTOUCHED at **v40**. **DML ONLY â€” `email_templates` id 216 inserted then edited once, no DDL**, committed as a migration file per #196, so the security advisor was correctly **NOT** run. `deno check --no-lock` **0**. `npm run build` **exit 0, 556 modules, 33 route pages** (was 32). The end-to-end reset was **tested live by the user against v716 and PASSED**. **The 5-pipeline smoke gate is PENDING-USER and REQUIRED â€” `dispatch.ts` was edited.** **`npm run deploy` is OWED â€” none of the frontend half is live.** Gotchas **#354**, **#355**, **#356**, all three ALWAYS-APPLIES; **#325 amended in place** (ten â†’ eleven auto-send rows). **MERGE-PENDING (both repos).**)
  - **WHAT STARTED IT, AND WHY THE OBVIOUS SUSPECT WAS WRONG.** Tax planner **Katie Williams** (`tax_planner_logins` id 8) had been locked out repeatedly across several password resets, which reads exactly like a broken hash write. It was not. `hashPasscodeSalted`/`verifyPasscodeSalted` are symmetric; her reset **provably wrote** (the hash changed) and her fresh login **provably succeeded** (an `admin_sessions` row seconds after the token's `completed_at`); and `login_attempts` held **7 genuine wrong-password failures on 2026-08-10 between 18:36 and 18:54 UTC** â€” a client sending the wrong string, not a server rejecting the right one. **The cause was the login FORM.** All five login pages rendered their inputs with no `id`, no `name` and no `autoComplete`, so a password manager had nothing to key a saved entry on and could never offer to *update* it after a reset â€” it just kept re-filling the dead passcode, and the 5-per-15-minutes throttle turned that into a hard lockout. The precedent was already on file and had been misread: planner `cgrover` needed a second setup link the day after the first, same loop. Gotcha **#354**.

All three strings were **arithmetically correct** and matched the backend exactly — `perPull = round(8000/12) = $667`, `pullsAtLink = 1 + max(0, remaining − slots)`, totals invariant at `remaining × 667`. The bug was not in the numbers; it was that **a number computed on one date was being presented as a fact about another**.
  - **THE DECAY (#349).** `transferLinkPulls(plan, basisDate)` is a function of its basis date, and four surfaces pass three different ones: the preview passes the admin's browser today, `send-setup-link` passes the day the email is drafted, and `setup-load`/`setup-checkout`/`activate` pass **the real pay date**. `remaining` is fixed at plan save; `slots` shrinks toward the fixed renewal. Nothing is ever mischarged — the page and Stripe recompute live — but **the emailed number is stale on arrival**, and the member sees double what their email promised.
  - **THE BOUNDARY THAT LOOKS LIKE AN OFF-BY-ONE AND ISN'T (#350).** The Aug 15 cliff is one day earlier than "after the 15th" would suggest, because a charge date landing **exactly on** the renewal 15th is dropped by `untilExclusive`. That drop is **load-bearing**: the renewal sweep treats any row with `due_date >= renewal_date` as an already-generated year 2, so an inclusive boundary would make the plan skip its renewal **forever** and quietly stop billing. Year 2's first pull legitimately lands on the renewal date instead (sweep runs renewals before charges in the same pass, so it is created and charged the same day).

  - **WHAT SHIPPED.** Backend: `annualTransfer` flag → selects new template **`MEMBERSHIP_transfer_setup_link|annual` (id 215)**; `remainingCount` falls back to **1** not 12 for annual; the button label on any `saveOnly` link reads *"Save Your Payment Method"* instead of promising a payment. Holistic now has the real step: **NEW `program_client_tasks` id 175**, `phase_id=18`, `task_order=1`, `status_options='tax_returns_request'` — the FIRST step of Tax 1 - Diagnostic, matching program 4's shape.   - **HOLISTIC STAMPING IS REQUEST-GATED, AND THAT GATE IS THE WHOLE REASON OLD EMAILS STAY INERT (#340, Option A, the user's explicit choice).** `clients.tax_upload_token` is **durable and shared** — every `/tax-upload` link already sitting in a client's inbox from a pre-v709 first-payment email is the SAME URL the new step mints. So `actions/vault/upload-notify.ts` could not simply start stamping Holistic plans: it would have retro-greened a step for clients who were never asked. It is now **DUAL-CANDIDATE** — the newest program-4 plan is selected unconditionally (unchanged semantics), and the newest Holistic plan (`.or("program_id.is.null,program_id.eq.1")` — `.eq` would exclude the NULL legacy rows) is selected **only when `tax_returns_requested_at` is set**. Every unstamped candidate gets `tax_returns_received_at`; the `TAX_returns_received` bell fires **exactly ONCE**; a client holding plans in BOTH programs gets **both** stamped by one upload. An upload from a client with no requested plan still falls through to the original generic FYI, untouched. **This supersedes the #269/GOTCHAS claim that `tax_returns_received_at` is hard-gated to `program_id = 4`** — that clause has been corrected in place in both the curated list and #269 itself.
  - **THE DUAL-CANDIDATE SHAPE WAS A BUG FIX, NOT THE ORIGINAL DESIGN — v710 EXISTS BECAUSE OF IT.** v709 shipped the Holistic candidate as an `else` to the program-4 lookup, so a client holding plans in both programs had program 4 **swallow** the upload and the Holistic plan never went green. Found in click-testing, fixed in v710 by making the two lookups independent and the stamp a loop. Worth remembering: "newest plan" selection across a two-program client is never a single query.
  - **THE EMAIL WORDING IS PER-PROGRAM AND THE TEMPLATE NAME HAS TO TRAVEL WITH IT.** `actions/tax/request-returns.ts` now selects on `(plan.program_id || 1) === 1` → **`TAX_request_returns|holistic`** (`email_templates` **214**, NEW, Draft mode like its base row 194, same recipients, body identical except a user-approved opening line naming the VFO Services Membership), **with a fallback to the base `TAX_request_returns`** if the variant row is missing or inactive. The react half mirrors the same ternary in the step's `StepEmailsChip`, and `templateMeta.js` gained the matching entry so the chip can describe it.

- **Producing the ROI presentation for a tax client used to be a human assembling a deck by hand out of numbers that were already sitting in the plan — the Tax 2 - Deeper Dive phase now has a button that fills the master deck, converts it to a real Google Slides file and hands back a link; and the one figure the deck always needed but nobody had ever been asked for, “Total Taxes without a Tax Plan”, became a REQUIRED field on the assess form in the same change** (2026-08-06, branch `claude/vfo-session-setup-0ecab1` in **BOTH** repos — edge = **1 NEW + 4 modified code files + 1 NEW migration file**, react = **2 modified code files** + docs. **+1 action (457)** = `tax_generate_presentation` (**AUTH**, `ADMIN_ONLY_ACTIONS`). `deno check --no-lock` **0** after the edge edits, **again after the mid-session `git merge origin/main`**, and once more at this audit. **Backend DEPLOYED TWICE — v705 (STALE, superseded, an incident recorded below) then v706 (GOOD, verified ACTIVE via MCP `list_edge_functions`)**, both deploys user-approved. `boldsign-webhook` UNTOUCHED at **v40**. **ONE MIGRATION, applied live via MCP AND committed as a file (#196)**, security advisor after the DDL → **GREEN**. **NEW private storage bucket `presentation-templates`.** Gotchas **#336** (ALWAYS-APPLIES — tax track) **+ #337** (ALWAYS-APPLIES — deploy/ops). **Pipeline smoke gate RUN by the user vs v706 — 5/5 PASS**, and the feature was click-tested end to end against live data. **DEPLOY/TAG DEBTS SINCE SETTLED — re-derived from git at the 2026-08-07 SECOND-session audit: the frontend WAS deployed and tagged `live-130-roi-presentation`, and `backend-good-2026-08-06-v706` exists**, so the assess-form 400 window this entry warned about is closed.)
  - **WHAT THE BUTTON ACTUALLY DOES, END TO END.** `tax_generate_presentation` (`actions/tax/generate-presentation.ts`) reads the plan, its `assess_form` and the plan-level risk grade, pulls the tokenized master **`ROI-template-master.pptx`** out of the new private **`presentation-templates`** bucket, substitutes **13 `{{TOKENS}}`** across slides **1 / 20 / 23 / 24 / 25 / 27** (every value XML-escaped before it goes near the slide XML), **repositions the slide-20 `upArrow`** to the client’s risk band off a hardcoded EMU table (1→801612, 2→2566499, 3→4349395, 4→6126289, 5→7900180 — the numbers came from measuring the chevron strip PNG, they are not guesses), then uploads the result to **Google Drive multipart with metadata `mimeType='application/vnd.google-apps.presentation'`**, which is what makes Drive **convert it server-side into a real Google Slides file** rather than parking a .pptx. It lands in an **“ROI Presentations”** folder under `GOOGLE_DRIVE_FOLDER_ID`, gets sharing **role=writer type=anyone**, and the handler stamps `client_tax_plans.generated_presentation_{drive_id,url,at,by}` and returns `{success, url, generated_at}`. **The formulas are fixed and worth having written down:** `gross = Σ(gross_y1+gross_y2)`; `invest = Σ(invest_y1+invest_y2)`; `taxes_with = taxes_without − gross`; `net = gross − invest − fee`; `outlay_plus_fee = invest + fee`; `fee_half = fee/2`; `pct = round(gross/taxes_without × 100)`; `year` = the **current calendar year at generation time**. Money renders whole-dollar with commas (`fee_half` drops to 2 dp only when it is genuinely fractional) and negatives use accounting parentheses. The risk grade is the **plan-level** `client_tax_progress` row (`tax_specialist_id IS NULL`) for the task “Client risk profile complete”, parsed `/Risk\s*([1-5])/`.
  - **THE ZIP WORK IS THE PERFORMANCE STORY, AND IT INTRODUCED THE FIRST ZIP LIBRARY THIS CODEBASE HAS EVER HAD.** A .pptx is a zip, and this one is **27.6 MB — almost entirely PNGs**. The handler uses **fflate** (`https://esm.sh/fflate@0.8.2`), and the pattern that makes it viable is: **re-store every untouched entry at level 0 and deflate ONLY the 6 edited slide XMLs**. Recompressing the whole archive would burn most of a minute on image data that did not change. That is also why `src/lib/api.js` gained a **`LONG_TIMEOUT_ACTIONS` map** giving this one action **90s** instead of the default — generation runs ~30–60s in practice. **The #30 rule was left completely intact: writes still never retry**; only the timeout is per-action.

The requirement is enforced by `actions/tax/save-assess-form.ts` **and** by `AssessTaxForm` inside `TaxPrioritiesTab.jsx` with the **identical message** — *“Total Taxes without a Tax Plan is required”* — so the pair must move together or the two halves disagree. The generator adds two of its own 400s on top: **≤ 0** → *“Total Taxes without a Tax Plan must be greater than zero”* (it is a divisor), and a **legacy submission that predates the field** → *“Re-save the Assess form — it was submitted before the Total Taxes field existed”*, which tells the admin exactly what to do rather than failing opaquely.

**Archived CURRENT STATE entry — the 2026-08-04 THIRD session (membership renewal notice + meeting flow + Pause Membership Payments, backend v703), verbatim.**

- **A membership renewal used to arrive with no warning whatsoever — the plan simply rolled into another year and the charge showed up — so members now get a 30-day advance notice carrying a "Request a Meeting" button, and the requests land in an action-required queue that an ACCOUNTING admin rather than a superadmin works; and separately, a membership can now be PAUSED for a few months without the plan ever leaving `active`, because a pause was modelled as a schedule shape plus a renewal date instead of as a new status** (2026-08-04, the **THIRD** session that day, branch `claude/vfo-session-setup-891daa` in **BOTH** repos — edge = **3 new + 4 modified code files + 2 new migration files**, react = **6 modified + 1 new code file** + docs. **+3 actions (456)** — `membership_renewal_meeting_request` (**PUBLIC**), `membership_renewal_meeting_outcome` (**AUTH, accounting-tab**), `membership_pause` (**AUTH, superadmin**). `deno check --no-lock` **0** after every edge edit and again at this audit. **Backend DEPLOYED FOUR TIMES → live `vfo-admin-api` v703** (v699 → v700 → v701 → v702 → v703, every deploy user-approved; v703 re-verified **ACTIVE** via MCP `list_edge_functions` at this audit). `boldsign-webhook` UNTOUCHED at **v40**. **TWO MIGRATIONS — applied live via MCP AND committed as files (#196)** — and the **Supabase security advisor was RUN after BOTH and is GREEN**, with anon probes `*/0` on both new tables. Gotchas **#332** (ALWAYS-APPLIES, money) **+ #333** (ALWAYS-APPLIES) **+ #334**. **All three features were live-tested end to end by the user against v700/v702; the pipeline smoke gate was run by the user vs v700 — 5/5 PASS.** **The FRONTEND IS NOT DEPLOYED — `npm run deploy` is owed.** **MERGE-PENDING both repos.**)
  - **THE HONEST FINDING CAME BEFORE THE FEATURE: MEMBERSHIP RENEWAL WAS COMPLETELY SILENT.** The research half of this session established that nothing anywhere warned a member that their membership was about to renew. The sweep rolled the plan into its next year the moment `renewal_date` arrived — new ledger, next-year terms applied, charging resumed — and `auto_renew` is `true` by default on every plan. **A member's first signal that they had been committed to another year was the charge on their statement.** That is what pass 0 closes, and it is worth recording that the gap was nine months old and had never been framed as one.
  - **THE IDEMPOTENCY STAMP IS THE LOAD-BEARING PART OF THE NOTICE PASS, AND ITS ORDERING IS DELIBERATE (#333).** `sweep.ts` gained a **pass 0** that runs BEFORE the renewal pass, so a plan is always warned before it is rolled over. Window: `status='active'` + `auto_renew` + `renewal_date` in `(today, today+30]` — **strictly future**, so a plan that actually reaches its 15th is renewed by pass 1 rather than noticed. The "already noticed" test is `renewal_notice_for <> renewal_date` and is evaluated **in JS**, because PostgREST cannot compare two columns and NULL has to read as not-noticed. The new `member_payment_plans.renewal_notice_for` is written **ONLY after the Gmail draft actually succeeds** — a missing template, a token refresh failure or a member with no email simply leaves it alone and retries tomorrow. Stamping first would have turned every transient Gmail hiccup into a permanently skipped notice. Because the predicate is an inequality, the pass also **re-arms automatically whenever the renewal date moves** — including after a pause. The durable `renewal_meeting_token` (partial-unique) is minted once per plan, reused by every subsequent notice, and **persisted BEFORE the email is drafted** so a link that goes out always resolves. `summary.noticed` joins the sweep's counters.
  - **`[Renewal Terms]` IS THE RENEWAL PASS'S OWN ARITHMETIC WRITTEN A SECOND TIME, AND A MISMATCH WAS CAUGHT IN REVIEW.** The notice quotes `(next_year_amount ?? annual_amount) − (next_year_credit_note ?? 0)` — **exactly** what pass 1 will bill. An earlier draft computed it differently; that was found during adversarial review of the money path and fixed before the deploy. **Quoting a member a renewal price the system then does not charge is the worst failure this feature has available to it**, so the two copies are now explicitly noted as having to move together.
  - **THE MEETING REQUEST IS A ONE-BIT PUBLIC ENDPOINT AND THE BELL HAS EXACTLY ONE EXIT.** NEW `actions/membership/renewal-meeting-request.ts` (`membership_renewal_meeting_request`, **PUBLIC**, in `PUBLIC_HANDLERS` with a comment) is credentialed **entirely** by `renewal_meeting_token` and returns a **bare `{ success }` that must never be widened** — the same reasoning as #331, stated in a file comment. It is **idempotent per `(plan_id, renewal_date_for)` open row**, so a double-click or a re-opened email renders the "already received" state instead of queueing a second meeting. It inserts a `membership_renewal_meetings` row and fires `notifyByRule('MEMBERSHIP_renewal_meeting_requested')` — **action-required (`dismissible:false`)**, default recipient `rhopson@elitert.com`, linked straight to the member's Membership Fees card. NEW `actions/membership/renewal-meeting-outcome.ts` stamps `completed_at` / `outcome` / `recorded_by`; **`cancel` also flips `auto_renew=false` and drafts `MEMBERSHIP_cancel_confirmation` inside a `try/catch`** (a Gmail failure must not lose an outcome that is already recorded); **both outcomes clear the bell**, and nothing else does.
  - **THE GATE MOVED ON PURPOSE AND MONEY DID NOT MOVE WITH IT (#333).** `membership_plans_load` **lost its in-handler superadmin check** — it is a read-only loader, and `TAB_ACTIONS.accounting` is now its whole gate, exactly like `accounting_outstanding_links_load`. `membership_renewal_meeting_outcome` was **never given one**. Both exceptions are commented at their sites in `role-gates.ts` and in `plans-load.ts` specifically so a future reader of #309 does not "restore" a check that was removed deliberately. The reason is a person: **Rachael Hopson runs the renewal meetings and is not a superadmin.** Correspondingly the two Membership Fees mounts in `AdminPortal.jsx` relaxed from `session.is_superadmin` to `canSeeTab('accounting')`, and `MembershipFeesPanel.jsx` now takes an `isSuperadmin` prop behind which **every money control** sits — create/setup, links, auto-renew, next-year terms, Pause, Terminate, cancel, resend/reminder. An accounting-tab admin sees read-only cards, the schedule and the Renewal meeting section, and nothing that spends money.

The client half navigates to `/admin/client/<id>` with optional `?program=`/`&tab=`. The `_n` cache-buster is stamped **inside the onClick**, not at render, because AdminPortal reads `window.location.search` — two clicks on the same member without an intervening re-render must still differ.
  - **THREE SMALL CONTRACTS THAT WILL BITE THE NEXT PERSON.** (1) `style={{ ...style, ...baseStyle }}` — the helper's `baseStyle` spreads **LAST**, so **a passed `color` is dead**; callers pass only `fontSize`/`fontWeight`. (2) Both components `e.stopPropagation()` on click, which is what lets them sit inside expandable card headers and clickable table rows without hijacking the row. (3) A **falsy id renders a plain `<span>`** — the deliberate fallback for rows whose id genuinely does not exist yet (a pre-stage-3 onboarding), so call sites never need a guard.

  - **FIVE STATUSES, AND THE ORANGE ONE IS THE WHOLE POINT (#318).** `complete` (green, "Account Set up") requires `payouts_enabled` **AND** `capabilities.transfers==='active'` **AND** `currently_due` + `eventually_due` **both empty** — only that is finished. **`eligible_capped` (orange, "Account setup — payouts eligible to $3,000")** is the state nobody had a name for: payable *today*, but with requirements outstanding that will stop payouts at the $3,000 lifetime threshold. It is deliberately NOT green. `pending` (red) = payouts or transfers not enabled. **`mode_mismatch` (gray) is a real condition, not an error** — Connect accounts live under whichever sandbox/live toggle was active when they were created, so the handler retries the id under the OTHER key and, if it resolves there, renders a neutral "Status unavailable (account created in sandbox/live mode)". **A red or green dot must be earned from a live Stripe read; a mode-mismatched id degrades to gray rather than sending an admin chasing a member whose account is perfectly fine on the other platform.** `unavailable` (gray) covers Stripe unreachable or 404 under both keys.
  - **THE $3,000 CAP WAS BEING BUILT INTO EVERY LINK WE SENT (#317).** This is the bug behind the orange state, and it was in the link minting, not the UI. `POST /v1/account_links` asks the account holder only for what is **currently** blocking them; the SSN and date of birth Stripe demands at the $3,000 lifetime-payout threshold sit unrequested in `eventually_due`. So a member clicked our setup link, was shown an already-complete page, and reasonably concluded they were done — until their payouts stopped months later. **Both mints now append `collection_options[fields]=eventually_due`**: `actions/payouts/connect-setup-link.ts` (which backs the durable `/payout-setup?token=` page and therefore covers **all four** entity types — member, specialist, strategic group, tax planning group, #268) and `utils/specialist-revenue-payout.ts` (the automatic SPECREV "awaiting connect" email, #159). **That fix is already live and needs no frontend** — every link minted since v693 collects the full set. It does **not** retroactively repair accounts already onboarded through an old link; those are exactly the ones that now show orange, and they need a resend.
  - **THE EMAIL WAS TOLD THE TRUTH TO MATCH.** `email_templates` id 159 (`member_connect_setup`) now says, as a plain paragraph rather than 12px gray fine print, *"This one-time setup takes about 5 minutes — Stripe will ask for your personal details, including your SSN and date of birth, so you're fully set up for life."* Since the link genuinely does ask for those things now, burying the warning would have been the wrong half of the fix. The `<br><br>` before `[SETUP_LINK]` was dropped in the same pass (link paragraph top margin 24px → 16px).
