A NEW always-visible **"Stripe Connect"** section sits in **MemberSettings**, between Member Login and the Danger Zone: no account → helper + a primary **"Set Up Payment Details"**; account → the chip + an outline **"Resend setup email"**. The **Details** view keeps the observation half — account chip + the status pill + a Refresh text-button. **Act in Settings, observe on Details** — a future Connect surface should follow the same split. `MemberSettings` holds its own local request state and calls `member_stripe_connect_request` then `onDataChange()`, which re-syncs `selectedMember` from `allMembers` (`MembersPanel.jsx` ~line 346); the no-account branch on Details is unchanged, and its `sendStripeRequest → loadProfile()` still flips the view to the connected layout on its own.

  - **WHY THE OLD FORM WAS WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS.** A mid-year transfer keeps its existing renewal 15th, and the schedule used to be derived purely from that date: bill every charge date before renewal, one pull at the link, done. That is only correct for a member who is exactly on schedule. A member who came in with **free weeks** (paid ahead on the old platform) got billed for months they had already covered; a member who was **behind** got billed fewer than 12 times in the year and simply never caught up, because the renewal date is fixed and there are only so many charge dates before it. The admin had no way to say which of the two was happening, and the form's numbers and the emails' numbers were derived independently, so they could disagree.
  - **ONE INPUT, EVERYTHING ELSE DERIVED — and the derivation lives in exactly one function.** `prior_payments_made` (0–11) is now **REQUIRED** on monthly transfers (`plan-save.ts` 400s with *"Enter how many payments they already made this year (0-11)"*; still optional on annual transfers, which pay nothing at the link). The NEW column `member_payment_plans.remaining_payments` is **DERIVED SERVER-SIDE as `12 − prior`** and is written **unconditionally** — any value a client sends is ignored, and editing a plan away from monthly/transfer clears it back to NULL rather than leaving a stale number behind. NEW exported **`transferLinkPulls(plan, basisDate)`** in `actions/membership/shared.ts` returns `{remaining, slots, pullsAtLink}` and is the **single source** consumed by all four surfaces that used to compute their own answer: `setup-load.ts` (what the `/membership-pay` page shows), `setup-checkout.ts` (what Stripe actually charges), `activate.ts` (what the ledger records) and `send-setup-link.ts` (what the email quotes). `slots = 1 + subsequentChargeDates(basis, {untilExclusive: renewal}).length`; `remaining` falls back to `slots` when the column is NULL, which reproduces the **exact** legacy behaviour for any pending plan saved before the column existed; `pullsAtLink = 1 + max(0, remaining − slots)`.
  - **BEHIND PAYS CATCH-UP AT THE LINK; AHEAD JUST STOPS EARLY; THE RENEWAL DATE NEVER MOVES.** That is the whole model in one line. A member owing more than the calendar has room for pays the shortfall **in the first payment** — `mode=payment` charges `pullsAtLink × base` (the New Model card gross-up wraps the **total**, not the base), the memo appends *" (includes N-month catch-up)"*, and the period label reads *"August 2026 (includes 1-month catch-up)"*. A member with free weeks simply gets fewer scheduled rows and nothing at all in the months already covered. Because the year still ends on the same 15th, renewal, next-year terms and the sweep's renewal guard (#235) are all untouched.
  - **THE CATCH-UP MUST BE ONE ROW, AND WE LEARNED THAT THE EXPENSIVE WAY (#315).** The first implementation wrote the catch-up as **k separate rows all dated the pay date**. `member_payment_schedule` carries a deliberate **UNIQUE `(plan_id, due_date) WHERE kind='membership'`** index — the duplicate-charge guard — so in the sandbox test **Stripe collected the money first** and the year-1 ledger insert then bounced on `23505`: plan stuck `setup_pending`, member paid, no ledger, only an alert bell. It now folds into **ONE** row at `perPull × pulls` with `credit_applied` scaled the same way. That is safe because **the invoice/receipt engine totals by PaymentIntent, not by row** — a combined charge already stamps one PI (and one `card_processing_fee`, #281) across every row it covers. Two adjacent traps were closed in the same rewrite: a follow-up remainder of **0 must short-circuit** (`count: 0` is falsy inside `subsequentChargeDates` and reads as UNLIMITED), and `untilExclusive: renewalDate` is now passed on **every** transfer branch including the counted one, so no scheduled row can ever land on or after the renewal date.
  - **COUNTS SPEAK IN MONTHS NOW, NOT ROWS (#316).** The moment a row could span several months, `rowsThisYear.length` stopped meaning "payments remaining" — the invoice said **6** where the setup email said **7**, and the schedule ended the year at **"Payment 11"** of 12. NEW **`monthsCoveredByRow(row, grossMonthly)`** = `max(1, round((amount_due + credit_applied) / grossMonthly))` derives a row's span from the row's **own money**, which is what makes it survive a credit spread: net alone is short by the credit, but **net + credit = one gross month**. `invoice-receipt.ts` now routes every count through it — the invoice's payments-remaining, each schedule-line ordinal (multi-month rows label as **ranges**, *"Payments 6-7"*, so the year reaches 12), the receipt's `paymentLabel`, and the `[Remaining Payments]` / `[X]` / `[Y]` tokens. `utils/membership-confirmation.ts` counts the transfer ordinal's denominator the same way. **An ordinary row always evaluates to 1, so every non-catch-up document is byte-identical to before** — that is the regression proof, not an assertion.
  - **THE SETUP EMAIL NOW QUOTES THE REAL NUMBER.** `send-setup-link.ts` sources `[Remaining Payments]` from `transferLinkPulls` (it used to re-derive it from the renewal date) and gained **`[Setup Amount]`** — the actual link total — and **`[Setup Note]`**, which expands to *" — this covers N months (your regular month plus N-1 catch-up month(s)) so you're fully caught up by your renewal"* and is **empty when there is only one pull**, so a normal transfer's email is unchanged. Template id 191 was edited to consume both.
  - **ONE PRE-EXISTING WEBHOOK BUG RODE ALONG, AND ONE ALERT WAS TOLD THE TRUTH.** In the **MEMBER MEMBERSHIP FEES setup-link block only**, `router/webhooks.ts` now reads the session's `pull_count` metadata (stamped on **both** the session and `payment_intent_data`, clamped `>= 1`) and multiplies the **card-fee base** and the **ACH confirmation amount** by it. Without that, a multi-pull payment would have stamped the entire extra pull as `card_processing_fee` — and the invoice/receipt engine deliberately **prefers the stamped fee** over any re-derivation (#281), so the wrong number would have printed on a real document. `pipeRow` and every other webhook block are untouched. Separately, the activation-failure alert was **reworded**: the title is now *"Membership payment received but NOT recorded — <name>"* (payment path) / *"Membership setup saved but plan NOT activated"* (save-only) and the message opens *"The member's first payment WENT THROUGH at Stripe — the money landed — but it is not recorded on the ledger"*. The old *"Membership activation FAILED"* was read as a failed charge by the user during live testing — exactly the wrong instinct at exactly the wrong moment.
  - **THE FRONTEND FORM LOST INPUTS ON PURPOSE.** `MembershipFeesPanel.jsx`'s monthly-transfer setup is now **one required field** — *"Payments already made this year"* (0–11, blocks save when blank or invalid) — with everything else mirrored from the backend (`remaining = 12 − prior`, `pullsAtLink = 1 + max(0, remaining − slots)`, `perPull = max(0, roundDollar(annual/12 − credit/remaining))`) and rendered as a plain-English preview: *"Paid 5 of 12 — 7 × $667.00 left: $1,334.00 at the link (includes 1-month catch-up), then 5 monthly until renewal Jan 15, 2027"*. **CURRENT STATE entry archived verbatim from SESSION_REFERENCE (the member Introductions-vs-Connections session, aged out at this audit):**
- **"Connected Member" splits into TWO different relationships that were never the same thing — an INTRODUCTION is one-way and carries the tier the INTRODUCER earns, a CONNECTION is mutual, untyped and unlimited — and both now render on BOTH members' profiles with clickable names, while the old single-pointer column retires to corporate-parent duty** (2026-07-31, the SECOND session that day, branch `claude/vfo-session-setup-b5c9b3` in **BOTH** repos — edge = **4 modified + 2 new action files + 2 new migration files**, react = **2 code files** + docs. **+2 actions (449)** — `member_connection_add` + `member_connection_remove`. `deno check --no-lock` **0** after every edge edit. `npm run build` exit 0, 31 route pages. **Backend DEPLOYED → live `vfo-admin-api` v685** (TWO deploys, v684 then v685, both user-approved; verified via `list_edge_functions`). `boldsign-webhook` UNTOUCHED at **v40**. **TWO DDL migrations**, written as files AND applied live **by the user** in Studio SQL (the Claude-side MCP was permission-blocked — #196 still satisfied because the files are committed) → security advisor **GREEN** + anon probe `*/0`. Gotcha **#312** (ALWAYS-APPLIES). **MERGE-PENDING both repos.**)
  - **WHY.** There was exactly ONE member-to-member link in the system: `members.connected_member_number`, a single self-referencing pointer, optionally tiered by `members.connection_type`. That one slot was carrying three unrelated meanings — a revenue-sharing introduction, an ordinary peer relationship, and the corporate-parent pointer — and because it was one-way and single-valued it failed at all three: the *other* member's profile showed nothing, a second relationship overwrote the first, and nobody could tell from the data which meaning a given row had. The two real concepts now have two separate stores with two different shapes, and the old column keeps only the third meaning.
  - **AN INTRODUCTION IS DIRECTIONAL, AND THE TIER IS THE INTRODUCER'S MONEY (#312).** NEW column `members.introduced_by_member_number` (text, FK → `members.member_number` `ON DELETE SET NULL`) answers "who introduced THIS member" — **one introducer per member**. The tier stays in the EXISTING `members.connection_type` (`'5% - Regular Advisor'` / `'10% - Accredited Introducer'` / `'10% - Accredited Mentor'` / `'20% - Accredited Introducer + Mentor'`), relabelled **"Introducer Benefit"**, because it describes what the person named in `introduced_by_member_number` earns: **read it off the introduced member's row, pay it to the introducer.** It is now shown for **every** member category — accountants included, where the dropdown used to be hidden. Migration `20260731120000_introduced_by_member_number.sql` also MOVED the three rows that already carried a tier (Marjorie Wang 59470 ← Jason Bright 59119, Violetta Terpeluk 59515 ← Deb Snyder 59414, Todd Veillon 58088-FC6 ← Jack Branch 58088) — a typed old-style link WAS an introduction, which is exactly why `connection_type` could be reused untouched. **No new action was needed for this half**: `member_profile_save` is a whole-row spread upsert of the `profile` payload, so the column persists through the ordinary Save button.
  - **A CONNECTION IS A CANONICAL PAIR, AND THE CHECK IS THE DESIGN.** NEW table `public.member_connections` (`id` identity PK, `member_a`/`member_b` text FK → `members` `ON DELETE CASCADE`, `created_at`, **CHECK `member_a < member_b`**, **UNIQUE `(member_a, member_b)`**, deny-all RLS in the same migration per #141). Storing the lexicographically smaller number first means the same link can never exist twice in opposite orders and "are these two connected" is ONE symmetric lookup. **Every writer normalizes before touching the table.** NEW `member_connection_add` / `member_connection_remove` (`actions/members/connection-add.ts` / `connection-remove.ts`, AUTH, both in `ADMIN_ONLY_ACTIONS` on the line below `member_profile_save`, both registered in `AUTH_HANDLERS` right after it) accept `{member_a, member_b}` in either order, sort them, and are **idempotent on purpose** — add treats a `23505` unique violation as success (double-clicks, retries), remove treats a missing row as success (the end state is reached either way). Add validates non-empty / not-equal / both-exist with an error-destructured lookup (#187) so a DB failure can never masquerade as "member not found".
  - **`connected_member_number` IS NOW LEGACY, AND THE VALUES ARE GONE.** Migration `20260731130000_member_connections.sql` backfilled all **240** one-way links as pairs and then **CLEARED the column on every non-corporate row** — zero live rows carry a value. It survives for exactly one writer: the Add Advisor **corporate** flow (`add_member_full`, behind the "Connected Member \*" picker that only appears for a Corporate member type), which uses it as the parent pointer; corporate members were deliberately excluded from both the backfill and the clear. `load_data` still returns it for that purpose. **Anything else reading it for connection meaning is now a bug, not a style question — the data is empty.** The PFT auto-link in `actions/accountant/create-member.ts` was converted accordingly: it no longer writes `connected_member_number` on the members insert and instead inserts a normalized pair **after** the members row exists (both sides are FKs), best-effort inside try/catch with `23505` swallowed, so a connection failure can never block accountant creation.
  - **THE PAYLOAD GAINED A TOP-LEVEL KEY, NOT A PER-MEMBER ONE.** `actions/data/load-data.ts` adds `introduced_by_member_number` to the per-member roster merge (beside `connected_member_number`/`connection_type` — a new `members` column is invisible to the portal until it is whitelisted there, #207) **and a NEW top-level `member_connections` array** of raw `{member_a, member_b}` rows, fetched by one extra query inside the existing `Promise.all`. Pairs are top-level rather than folded into each member because they are symmetric — attaching them per-member would duplicate every row twice and invite one side to drift.
  - **TWO CARDS ON DETAILS, AND THE DIRECTION IS SPELLED OUT.** The profile details view renders an **"Introductions"** card with two labelled sub-sections — *Introduced By* (this member's introducer, 40px avatar, tier chip **inline next to the name**) and *Introducer Of* (everyone whose `introduced_by_member_number` points back at this member, 30px rows, each chipped with **their own** `connection_type`) — plus a separate **"Connections"** card of mutual partners as plain rows with **no chips**, because a connection has no tier and inventing one would imply money that does not exist. Corporate-type members are excluded from both; they stay in the unchanged Corporate Members card.
  - **THE EDIT TAB HAS TWO ADJACENT CARDS WITH TWO DIFFERENT COMMIT MODELS — this is the trap (#312).** The **Introductions** card is ordinary buffered profile state (typeahead → `introduced_by_member_number`, select → `connection_type`, "Remove Introduction" clears both) and commits on **Save**, like every other card on the tab. The **Connections** card **cannot** — its data lives in another table — so each per-row **Remove** and each "Add Connection (search member)" pick fires `member_connection_remove` / `member_connection_add` **immediately** and then calls `onDataChange()` (`AdminPortal.loadAllData`) to re-read. **Leaving the tab without pressing Save does NOT undo a connection change.** The add typeahead also filters out existing partners and self, so the idempotent-add path is a safety net rather than a routine occurrence.

  - **WHY.** Tax 5 has been per-specialist since the specialist-allocation card shipped (#260/#305) — each allocated specialist gets their own education/DD box. Tax 6, the implementation phase that follows it, was still a SINGLE plan-level checklist: four steps answered once for the whole plan no matter how many specialists were implementing. That is wrong on its face — a plan can carry five specialists implementing five different strategies on different timelines, and one of them stopping says nothing about the other four. Tax 6 now mirrors Tax 5's shape exactly.
  - **THE STORAGE MOVE IS THE WHOLE CHANGE, AND IT IS BREAKING FOR OLD ROWS (#311).** The four Tax 6 tasks now live in `client_tax_progress` keyed by **`tax_specialist_id`** (progress key `${task.id}_${spec.id}`, saved through the existing `tax_save_task` with `tax_specialist_id` — no new action). **A plan-level (`tax_specialist_id` NULL) row for a Tax 6 task is therefore dead data** that no reader on either side will ever surface again. Eight such rows existed and were backed up and deleted (see the DB cell). **Every consumer of Tax 6 done-ness must iterate `client_tax_specialists`** — there are four, and they were all changed together: the FE `getPhaseState` branch, the FE hero counts, the FE card pill, and the BE overview branch. **Phase done additionally requires at least one allocated specialist** — a plan with none shows "No specialists allocated yet." and can never read Done, which is correct (nothing has been implemented) and is a deliberate change from the old vacuous-truth behavior.
  - **THE OVERVIEW SHARES TAX 5's SCOPE ON PURPOSE.** `overview-tax.ts` emits one step per specialist labelled `<task name> — <specialist name>` with `applicable: implReach`, and crucially tags it with the **SAME `spec-<id>` scope string the Tax 5 branch uses**. That makes one specialist's Tax 5 steps and their Tax 6 steps a single ordered sequence for the skipped-step scanner, so "step 3 answered but step 2 blank" warns within a specialist and never across two different specialists. Giving Tax 6 its own scope would have produced false warnings on every multi-specialist plan.
  - **CHIP PRECEDENCE IS Stopped > Done > In progress > Not started.** Per specialist box: ANY of the four steps answered `Stopped` → red **Stopped** (a stop is the headline, even if the other three are done); else all four answered → green **Done**; else some answered → blue **In progress · n/4**; else grey **Not started**. **"Answered" means any non-empty status** — `Completed`, `Stopped` and `N/A` all count, because the question has been decided either way. The box default-expands until all four are answered (expand key `tax6_spec_<id>`), matching the phase-collapse convention (#275). The card pill counts **specialists × 4**, not 4.
  - **THE HERO COUNT WAS THE EASY DOUBLE-COUNT TO GET WRONG.** Tax 6 is the only phase in `phasesAfterSpec`, and it used to be summed by the plan-level `reduce` over `[...phasesBeforeSpec, ...phasesAfterSpec]`. It is now **removed from BOTH reduces** and added once as its own per-specialist term (`taxSpecialists.length × tax6SpecTasks.length`), mirroring how `tax5aSpecTasks` is already handled. Leaving it in the reduce **and** adding the per-spec term would have counted it twice; removing it without adding the term would have dropped it from the hero entirely.
  - **THE REMOVE BUG THE USER HIT.** Removing a specialist left the card on screen until a page reload. `removeSpecialist` cleared the progress keys and the expand keys but relied on `loadSpecialists()` — whose `catch` is silent — to drop the row itself, so any hiccup in the re-fetch left a deleted specialist rendered. It now does an **optimistic `setTaxSpecialists(p => p.filter(...))` immediately after backend success**, with the re-fetch demoted to reconciliation. It also clears the new `tax6_spec_<id>` expand key alongside the Tax 5 `spec_<id>` one — a new per-specialist expand key must be cleared here or it leaks across specialist ids.
  - **CUSTOM NAMING: THE SERVER OWNS THE PREFIX.** The picker's trailing option is relabelled **"Custom"** (the sentinel `OTHER_SPEC_VALUE = '__other__'` is UNCHANGED) and selecting it reveals a name input (80-char `maxLength`) with **Add disabled until it is non-empty**. The body gains `custom_name`; `add-specialist.ts` runs `sanitizeCustomName` (collapse whitespace → trim → strip a leading case-insensitive "custom -" → 80-char cap) and inserts **`Custom - <name>`**, building the prefix itself from the `CUSTOM_PREFIX` constant so a client that sends "Custom - Bob" still stores `Custom - Bob` rather than doubling it. **An empty or absent `custom_name` falls back to the legacy `Other #N (See notes)` numbering** — kept deliberately for API back-compat and for rows already in the wild, not as a UI path (the FE can no longer reach it). **`expert_id` stays NULL on both paths**, so the showroom/widget-leak guarantee of #305 is untouched, and **neither path dedupes** (several customs on one plan are legitimate, exactly as several "Other"s were).
  - **WORDING.** The greyed-out Tax 5 steps under a `Client decision 2 = 'Move to Implementation'` plan now read **"(Due Diligence Skipped - Moved to Implementation)"** (was "(Moved to implementation)"). - **Any admin can now ASK a client, member or specialist for documents straight from the vault section that should hold them — one button drafts the email, the recipient uploads through a secure no-login link, and the files land in the right private bucket with a bell to Tray** (2026-07-30, the THIRD session that day, branch `claude/vfo-session-setup-8a783e` in **BOTH** repos — edge = **2 modified + 4 new files**, react = **10 modified + 2 new files** + docs. **+3 actions (447)** — `vault_request_docs` (AUTH) + `vault_request_upload_url` + `vault_request_upload_notify` (both PUBLIC). `deno check --no-lock` **0** after every phase. `npm run build` exit 0, **31 route pages**. **Backend DEPLOYED → live `vfo-admin-api` v681** (user-approved; verified via `list_edge_functions`) — **but a v682 was OWED for the Cc delta, and has since shipped.** `boldsign-webhook` UNTOUCHED at **v40**. **ONE DDL migration** (`20260730120000_vault_request_docs.sql`) applied via MCP **`apply_migration`** AND committed (#196 clean) → security advisor **GREEN** + anon probe `*/0`. Pipeline smoke gate vs v681 **5/5 PASS, run by the user**. Gotcha **#310** (ALWAYS-APPLIES, auth/security).)
  - **WHY.** The tax track already had "Request additional information" (#271/#308) — a button that emails a client a secure upload link — but it was welded to the tax pipeline and to `clients`. Everywhere else, asking someone for a document meant writing the email by hand and then chasing the reply attachment into the right vault folder by hand. This lifts the pattern out of tax and makes it a **utility of the vault itself**: six placements (client / member / specialist × Sensitive / General), no program, no pipeline, no step.
  - **THE DURABLE TOKEN IS THE NEW INFRASTRUCTURE (#310).** Members and specialists had **no public upload token at all** — only `clients.tax_upload_token` existed — so the feature could not simply reuse `/tax-upload`. NEW table `vault_upload_tokens` holds **ONE row per `(entity_type, entity_key, section)`**, minted with `token32()` on the first request and **reused on every resend** (stamping `last_requested_at`), so every email ever sent against a section keeps working. `unique (entity_type, entity_key, section)` is the durability guarantee; deny-all RLS is in the same migration (#141) and the anon probe returns `*/0`.
  - **THE PUBLIC PAIR IS TOKEN-GATED AND THE BODY SELECTS NOTHING.** `vault_request_upload_url` and `vault_request_upload_notify` are deliberately **PUBLIC and deliberately absent from every `role-gates.ts` list** — `constants/role-gates.ts` carries a comment saying so, precisely so the next reader of **#309** does not "fix" them. That is safe because the destination is derived **entirely server-side from the token row**: the minter reads `{entity_type, entity_key, section}` off the row, maps the bucket through `VAULT_REQUEST_BUCKETS` (client → `client-tax-returns`/`client-documents`, member → `member-tax-returns`/`member-vault`, specialist → `specialist-tax-returns`/`specialist-documents`) and writes to `${entity_key}/${rand16}_${safeName}`. **The body carries only `token` + `filename`** — never an id, a section or a bucket. #309 is satisfied by the same route `vault_tax_upload_url` satisfies it (PUBLIC + unguessable token), and **#310 is minted** to say so explicitly.
  - **ONE TEMPLATE FOR ALL THREE ENTITY TYPES, AND THE Cc IS AN UNSET ROLE TOKEN.** The seeded `email_templates` row (pipeline `VAULT`, `VAULT_request_documentation`, `to ["RECIPIENT"]`, **`cc ["MEMBER"]`**, `send_mode=false` = Draft) serves everyone. `vault_request_docs` resolves recipients with `RECIPIENT = the person` and `MEMBER = the client's member` **only when `entity_type === 'client'`**; member and specialist requests pass `null`, the role token resolves to nothing and the Cc list comes back empty. **"No Cc on member/specialist requests" is therefore achieved by OMISSION, not by a branch** — reusing this template for a new entity type means deciding its `MEMBER` ctx explicitly or it silently ships with no Cc.
  - **`/vault-upload` IS UPLOAD-ONLY ON PURPOSE.** `VaultUploadPage.jsx` is a `TaxUploadPage` clone with the "Or write an explanation" box **deliberately removed**: a typed answer only means something where a step is waiting on it (#308's shared received-stamp), and this feature hangs off a vault section, not a step. For the same reason **an upload arriving here fires NO tax stamps** — `tax_returns_received_at` / `additional_info_received_at` stay exclusively the `/tax-upload` flow's, so `/tax-upload` and `clients.tax_upload_token` are an untouched, separate system. The only signal this path raises is the new bell `VAULT_requested_doc_uploaded`, **to Tray alone**, wrapped in try/catch so a notification failure can never lose the file. `scripts/emit-route-pages.mjs` gained `vault-upload` (30 → **31 route pages**) so the emailed link is a real 200 on GH Pages rather than a SPA 404 (#295).
  - **THE SIX PLACEMENTS AND THE THREE PLACES THE BUTTON MUST NOT APPEAR.** `VaultSections.jsx` grew an optional per-section `requestDocs {entityType, entityKey, recipientName, recipientFirst}` — sections that don't pass it are byte-identical to before. `MemberVault.jsx` and `SpecialistAdminVault.jsx` attach it to their two default sections **only when `admin===true`**, so the member and specialist **self-portals never render it**; `ClientVaultTab.jsx` renders it when `sec.canManage && !readOnly`, which means the client's Sensitive section inherits the `isTaxAdmin` `canView` gate and a **tax planner's read-only view hides it**. The **ERT/VFOS third section never gets one** (#204 — admin-write/owner-read, out of scope). `RequestDocsButton.jsx` is self-contained: an inline compose card that **mirrors the seeded template byte-for-byte**, with the textarea sitting exactly where the typed text lands in the email, and a transient "Request email drafted" confirmation (8s). **The admin's typed request text is stored NOWHERE** — `[REQUESTED_INFO]` is interpolated into the draft and lost, unchanged from #271/#308.

  - **THE MONEY BUG — found by a fresh-eyes review, confirmed, and defused before it ever fired.** `actions/pipeline/contract-revshare.ts` and `actions/tax/revshare.ts` both opened with `let revPaidValue = "N/A — No Share Due"` — a **TERMINAL** status — and ran the Stripe transfer only inside `if (!isMoneyMapping && shareAmount > 0 && member.stripe_account_id)`. A share that WAS due but whose member had **no Connect account** (or a run where the `STRIPE_KEY` lookup failed) fell straight past that block and wrote the terminal value: **no transfer, no bell, and a row both sweeps treat as resolved**, indistinguishable from a genuine zero-share row. Replaced with an **exhaustive branch chain** — `isMoneyMapping` → `shareAmount <= 0` → `!stripe_account_id` (NEW non-terminal `AWAITING_CONNECT` = `"Awaiting Connect Setup"` + an action-required bell) → `!STRIPE_KEY` (`Failed` + the existing FAILURE bell) → transfer. NEW `utils/member-share-held.ts` holds the constant + the reconstructable `memberShareHeldTitle()` so the bell **self-clears** when the share finally pays, exactly like `PLANNER_SHARE_WITHHELD` (#284).
  - **THE HARD BLOCKER THE FIX ITSELF CREATED — and why the tax sweep had to move with it.** `actions/tax/revshare-sweep.ts` gated its retry on `isRetry = revShare === "Pending" || revPaid === "Failed"`, and the handler writes `rev_share='Completed - Revenue Share'` **even when held** — so a held tax leg would have matched NEITHER predicate and been dropped **forever**, a worse outcome than the bug. Widened with `|| revPaid === AWAITING_CONNECT` (reason label `awaiting-connect`). **The MAP 1 sweep needed NO change** — it has no `isRetry` gate. Alongside it: `*_rev_completed_at` is now stamped **only on a terminal outcome** (a held leg no longer reads as finished), `actions/tax/refund.ts` **settles** a held leg after a successful refund (else the widened sweep would pay a share out of refunded money), `actions/payments/normalize.ts` shows **"Awaiting payout setup"** instead of the misleading "Pending", and `actions/msm/pip-revshare.ts` got its missing-`STRIPE_KEY` hole closed (**PIP was the only pipeline already handling the missing-account case** — it still has no retry sweep, so its bell honestly says "manual re-fire").
  - **THE PAYOUT MATH + THE DEAD CONTRIBUTION CODE (#304).** The MAP 1 member leg computed `(member_share / gross_fee) × thisPayment`, so a member contribution making `net < gross` **silently shrank the entered share**. Now the entered share pays **IN FULL**, split by cumulative difference — **numerically identical for every existing row** (all have `gross == net` or a blank gross); the strategic leg's proration is untouched. **USER-CONFIRMED SEMANTICS:** `member_contribution` is a discount the member funds (client pays `gross − contribution`) and **Member Share is typed already net of it**, so both handlers' contribution-deduction blocks were **deleted** — they were dead (nothing has ever written `member_contrib_status='Pending'`) **and** a latent overpay-on-retry bug (they flipped the status to `Applied` **before** the transfer, so a retry recomputed without the deduction). `client_tax_plans` has no `member_contribution` column at all.

NEW `tax_remove_specialist` (admins **and** planners; guard order = load-by-id → **verify the row's REAL `tax_plan_id`** (#257) → `denyIfNotPlannerPlan`) **deletes the specialist's `client_tax_progress` rows FIRST** — the FK is `ON DELETE SET NULL`, and an orphaned NULL `tax_specialist_id` is the **PLAN-LEVEL** row `save-task.ts` finds via `.is(...,null)`, so a naive delete corrupts plan-level step state. `tax_add_specialist` gained an **idempotent-add guard** (same plan + same expert returns the existing row — the double-click fix at source) and the `other: true` path, which inserts a **NULL `expert_id`** with the server-controlled name **`Other #N (See notes)`**, numbered **max+1 per plan** so removing "#1" never makes the next add reuse "#2". A NULL expert means **no `experts` row exists**, so an "Other" can never leak into a showroom or the public widget. ONE picker (`TaxPrioritiesTab.jsx`) serves **both** programs, so both got it at once.

Two independent themes on branch `claude/vfo-session-setup-21c0c8` in BOTH repos. Edge = 10 code files + 2 migration files; react = 5 code files + docs. **+1 action (442)**, `deno check --no-lock` **0**, `npm run build` exit 0, backend deployed **v673 → v674 → v675**, `boldsign-webhook` untouched at v40. Gotchas **#303 / #304** (ALWAYS-APPLIES, money) and **#305** (tax track).

*Theme A — the silent revshare swallow.* Both member-share legs (`actions/pipeline/contract-revshare.ts`, `actions/tax/revshare.ts`) initialized `revPaidValue` to the TERMINAL `"N/A — No Share Due"` and ran the transfer only inside `if (!isMoneyMapping && shareAmount > 0 && member.stripe_account_id)`. A due share with no Connect account (or a failed `STRIPE_KEY` lookup) fell through and wrote that terminal value — never paid, never belled, never retried, and indistinguishable from a genuine zero-share row. Replaced with an exhaustive branch chain plus the new NON-terminal `AWAITING_CONNECT = "Awaiting Connect Setup"` and a self-clearing action-required bell (`utils/member-share-held.ts`, modelled on `PLANNER_SHARE_WITHHELD` / #284). The fix's own hard blocker: `actions/tax/revshare-sweep.ts`'s `isRetry = revShare === "Pending" || revPaid === "Failed"` would have dropped a held tax leg forever (the handler writes `rev_share='Completed - Revenue Share'` even when held), so it was widened with `|| revPaid === AWAITING_CONNECT`; the MAP 1 sweep has no such gate and needed nothing. Also: `*_rev_completed_at` gated on a terminal outcome, `actions/tax/refund.ts` settles a held leg after a refund, `actions/payments/normalize.ts` renders "Awaiting payout setup", and `actions/msm/pip-revshare.ts`'s missing-`STRIPE_KEY` hole closed (PIP already handled the missing-account case — the only pipeline that did — but has no retry sweep).

*Theme A2 — payout math + dead contribution code.* The MAP 1 member leg's `(member_share / gross_fee) × thisPayment` silently scaled the entered share down whenever a member contribution made `net < gross`; replaced with a cumulative-difference split that pays the entered share in full (numerically identical for every existing row). User-confirmed semantics: `member_contribution` is a discount the member funds and Member Share is entered already net of it. Both contribution-deduction blocks deleted — dead (nothing ever wrote `member_contrib_status='Pending'`) and a latent overpay-on-retry bug (status flipped to `Applied` before the transfer).

*Theme B — tax specialist allocation.* A double-click had created twin rows (Harritt, plan 72, rows 51/52, 240 ms apart) — no unique constraint, no delete path. NEW `tax_remove_specialist` (admins + planners, #257 parent-verification guard order) deletes the specialist's `client_tax_progress` rows FIRST, because the FK is `ON DELETE SET NULL` and an orphaned NULL `tax_specialist_id` collides with the plan-level row `save-task.ts` finds via `.is(...,null)`. `tax_add_specialist` gained an idempotent-add guard (the double-click fix at source) and the `other: true` path — a NULL `expert_id` with the server-controlled name `Other #N (See notes)`, numbered max+1 per plan, which by construction can never enter the specialists directory or a showroom. Migration `20260729210000_tax_specialist_other_option.sql` drops the `expert_id` NOT NULL.

That is fine for a human and useless for a crawler or a vendor reputation scanner, which sees the 404 or an empty shell. Public policy pages therefore had to be **real files in `public/`** (copied verbatim to the dist root, served with a genuine **200**, readable with JS disabled). - **Specialist $99/mo license invoice/receipt + Stage 4→5 automation fix** (2026-07-07, branch `claude/specialist-lic-invoice-fix` — backend only, `vfo-edge-functions`; **backend DEPLOYED v545→v550 across 6 approved deploys**, save-point tag **`backend-good-2026-07-07-v551`**; **DB applied live via MCP; advisor GREEN**; no frontend change). *(Moved from SESSION_REFERENCE CURRENT STATE 2026-07-08. Independently reviewed + hardened 2026-07-08 → v561; the claim RPC's migration file `20260708130000_claim_specialist_license_invoice_rpc.sql` was committed then — gotcha #196.)*
  - **Symptom.** Jake reported: specialist pays the $99/mo license via subscription checkout, gets the confirmation email, but the invoice/receipt email never drafts and the record never advances Stage 4→5 — a flow that had "worked ~30 times before." Stripe showed the webhook returning 200; nothing in the DB moved.
  - **Bug 1 — Stripe API version fragility (real, but not the root cause).** The `invoice.paid`/`invoice.payment_succeeded` handler hard-gated on the invoice's subscription ref (`invoice.subscription || invoice.parent?.subscription_details?.subscription`); the account's newer API version (`2025-08-27.basil`) can omit both, so the guard silently skipped the whole block. Fixed: never gate on the event's subscription ref — fall back to the row's stored `lic_subscription_id`. ALSO made the first invoice/receipt + Stage advance fire inline from `checkout.session.completed` (card path) by expanding the subscription's `latest_invoice` at checkout time, so the card-payment case no longer depends on a separate invoice event arriving/parsing correctly at all (ACH still waits for the later event, since funds aren't confirmed yet at checkout time).
  - **Bug 2 — THE actual root cause: a PostgREST schema-cache anomaly + a silently-swallowed error.** Direct REST calls (curl GET/PATCH) against `specialist_onboarding` resolved `lic_last_invoice_id` (added 2026-06-05) fine; the SAME write issued by the deployed edge function via `supabase-js` reliably threw `42703 column does not exist` — before AND after a `NOTIFY pgrst, 'reload schema'`. The ORIGINAL code destructured only `{ data }` from the claim UPDATE, so this real DB error was invisible — the handler just silently returned, looking identical to "nothing to do." This is almost certainly why it's been failing quietly for a while, not "just started" — the visible signal (confirmation email, a DIFFERENT code path) kept firing. **Fix:** every `supabase.from(...)` call in the license-invoice path now checks `error` and logs explicitly (gotcha #187); the specific troublesome write was moved into a new `SECURITY DEFINER` RPC `claim_specialist_license_invoice(p_onboarding_id, p_invoice_id, p_paid_at)` called via `supabase.rpc(...)` — RPC only needs PostgREST to resolve the function name (a coarser, stable cache entry), so the write now runs as native SQL with full column visibility, sidestepping the anomaly entirely (gotcha #188).
  - **Verification.** End-to-end on a fresh test specialist with a real sandbox card payment (`4242…`): invoice/receipt drafted (`INV-SPECLIC-…`/`REC-SPECLIC-…`), Stage 4→5 advanced automatically, claimed exactly once (idempotency intact — the `.or(is.null,neq)` dedup pattern, gotcha #28, is preserved inside the new RPC). Frontend: `components/admin/pip/PipMeetingsTab.jsx` (4th tab on Holistic clients, year-grouped meeting list, "+ Add Year" button, locked-meeting styling), `components/admin/pip/PipPurchaseDecisionForm.jsx` (3-decision dropdown + Pricing + Revenue Split per branch), `components/admin/PipAutomationPanel.jsx` (admin Automation Panel section, one row per PIP purchase, 5 collapsible step sections mirroring MAP 1), `pages/PipPayPage.jsx` (`/pip-pay` route, ACH/Card picker clone of `/pay`). State on `client_priority_tracks` (`track_type='pip'`) with 25 new `pip_*` columns: `pip_engagement_year`, `pip_scheduled_date`, `pip_completed_date`, `pip_paid`, `pip_purchase_kind` ('tax_planning'|'additional_pip'), `pip_purchase_pip_count`, `pip_purchase_gross`, `pip_purchase_member_contribution`, `pip_purchase_amount`, `pip_purchase_member_share`, `pip_purchase_vfos_share`, `pip_stripe_customer_id`, `pip_checkout_token`, `pip_payment_intent_id`, `pip_payment_status`, `pip_payment_method_type`, `pip_acct_last4`, `pip_card_processing_fee`, `pip_payment_completed_at`, `pip_payment_email_sent_at`, `pip_confirmation_email_sent_at`, `pip_invoice_number`, `pip_receipt_number`, `pip_invoice_drive_id`, `pip_receipt_drive_id`, `pip_invoice_receipt_email_sent_at`, `pip_rev_share_status`, `pip_rev_share_transfer_id`, `pip_rev_share_amount`, `pip_rev_share_completed_at`, `pip_rev_member_email_sent_at`, `pip_purchased_from_track_id` (FK back to source meeting for locked child meetings). Trigger graph: admin opens Holistic client's PIP Meetings tab → "+ Add Year" inserts N tracks (`pip_paid=true`) → admin clicks a meeting → Phase 3 "Purchase Additional Services (optional)" form submit (decision=No: no chain; decision=Tax Planning OR Additional PIP: fires `automation_PIP_stripecustomer` → `_paymentemail` chain; Additional PIP also creates N locked child meetings via `msm_add_pip_meetings_for_year(paid=false, source_track_id=X)`) → client clicks `/pip-pay?token=` → `_loadpayment` + `_stripecheckout` → Stripe Checkout (one-time only, NO `setup_future_usage`) → Stripe webhook routes by `metadata.pipeline='PIP'` + `metadata.payment_kind='purchase'` → cascade fallback after MAP1/Tax/Advisor → `_confirmationemail` + `_invoicereceipt` (PDFs uploaded to client's Drive folder, `INV-PIP-{clientRef}-{seq:0004}` / `REC-PIP-{clientRef}-{seq:0004}` from shared global `document_numbers` counter) + `_revshare` (Stripe Connect transfer for Revenue Share members; Money Mapping for MM members; same banner styling as MAP1/Tax). On Additional PIP success, revshare also unlocks locked child meetings (`UPDATE client_priority_tracks SET pip_paid=true WHERE pip_purchased_from_track_id=<source>`). **No Tracy's-sheet verification** — `pip_purchase_member_share`/`pip_purchase_vfos_share` are admin-entered at form-submit and trusted as-is. **No retry sweep** — failed Stripe Connect transfers need manual re-fire via service-role. 4 email templates (pipeline='PIP'): `PIP_meeting_confirmation`, `PIP_payment`, `PIP_confirmation`, `PIP_invoicereceipt_email`. See [docs/flows/pip-meetings.md](C:/vfo-react/docs/flows/pip-meetings.md) for the canonical end-to-end trace.
